Will Mohammed Shami help NDA woo Muslim voters?:RLD entry buzz after meeting Jayant; out of international cricket for 1.5 years
stories.summary: Away from international cricket, Mohammed Shami could be preparing to begin a new innings on the political pitch. Speculation about his possible entry into politics has intensified after his recent meeting with RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary. It is being discussed that the fast bowler could have two options ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The question now is whether his possible political entry is simply because of his popularity or whether it is part of a broader RLD-BJP strategy to reach Muslim voters in western Uttar Pradesh. Three reasons behind speculation over Shami’s political entry Shami has not yet retired from Indian cricket. This has raised questions over the timing of his possible entry into politics. According to political analysts, there are three reasons behind the speculation. 1. RLD could be a political bridge towards the BJP The RLD is currently part of the BJP-led NDA alliance. Directly joining the BJP could have raised several questions about Shami’s image among the Muslim community. In such a situation, the RLD, which has traditionally been associated with farmers, Jats and communal harmony, could serve as a more comfortable political bridge for Shami to enter the NDA camp. 2. Could he seek political backing amid legal issues? Shami’s younger brother, Mohammed Kaif, has been accused of rape by a woman from Lucknow. His family is facing legal complications in connection with the allegations. The source suggests that Shami could be looking to move closer to those in power to deal with possible pressure from the police and administration. 3. At 36, a long fast-bowling career may not be ahead Shami is a fast bowler and is now 36. The chances of a fast bowler being selected for the Indian cricket team tend to decline after the age of 35. Does the RLD want to make inroads into the SP’s Muslim vote base? Jayant Chaudhary’s party has largely remained centred around Jat and farmer politics. After joining hands with the BJP in the 2024 election, the RLD’s traditional “Jat-Muslim” equation is believed to have weakened to some extent. To counter the SP-Congress alliance led by Akhilesh Yadav, the RLD needs a prominent Muslim face, according to the source. Shami is not merely a Muslim face. He is a World Cup hero and a national icon, with a strong following among Muslim youth. Through Shami, the RLD could seek to send a message that despite being part of the NDA, it also speaks for the interests of the Muslim community. Shami could influence the Turk Muslim community Mohammed Shami is originally from Sahaspur Alinagar tehsil in Amroha district. Amroha, Moradabad, Sambhal, Bijnor, Meerut and Bulandshahr are identified in the source as his main areas of influence in western Uttar Pradesh. The Amroha seat has more than 3.25 lakh voters, of whom around 2 lakh are Muslim. More than 70,000 belong to the Turk community, which Shami’s family also comes from. SP heavyweight leader Mehboob Ali has held the Amroha seat since 2002. He also defeated BJP’s Ram Singh in 2022. If Shami or a member of his family becomes the face of the NDA, it could potentially challenge the SP’s hold over the seat. ‘Celebrity image’ could benefit Shami in politics The entry of cricket and Bollywood stars into Indian politics is not new. Mohammed Shami could benefit directly from his image as a sports star. His performances for India, particularly during the 2023 World Cup, made him popular among people across religious and social groups. Young voters who think beyond party lines or caste-based politics could be attracted by a popular sportsperson such as Shami, according to the source. The BJP-RLD alliance could also use his presence to project the message that it is not limited to any one community and is willing to include Muslim personalities who have brought recognition to the country. Expert says Shami’s entry may have limited impact on Muslim votes Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election is likely to be more bipolar than the 2022 and 2024 elections. According to him, the possibility of making significant inroads into Muslim votes through Mohammed Shami is very low. Kalhans says Shami is not a political face and that his popularity is also not what it once was. He believes contesting from Amroha would not automatically make it easy to secure votes with the support of the RLD-BJP alliance. According to him, Shami’s presence could certainly generate media attention and add glamour to the campaign, but its impact on votes is likely to be limited.

stories.title: Did DJ sound really cause girl’s death?:How sound waves can affect heartbeat; what is silent blockage?
stories.summary: A girl sitting in a classroom in Balrampur suddenly collapsed unconscious at her desk. She was taken to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. School authorities said a Ganesh immersion procession was passing by when she collapsed, and the DJ was playing so loudly that the classroom windows were shaking. It was suspected that the loud noise triggered a heart attack, leading to her death. The question is, What effect can extremely loud noise have on the body that it could potentially lead to death? And why would the sound affect only one girl in the classroom? Read today’s UP Explainer to find out… Question 1: Can loud DJ or sound-system music affect the heart and cause a heart attack? Answer: In simple terms, extremely loud sound can trigger a stress response, temporarily increasing heart rate and blood pressure. In vulnerable people, severe stress can contribute to cardiovascular complications. A. Sudden rise in stress hormones A sudden, very loud noise, such as a DJ bass or explosion-like sound, can be perceived by the brain as a threat. This can trigger the release of stress hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol, causing blood vessels to constrict and heart rate and blood pressure to rise. B. Abnormal heart rhythms The copy states that low-frequency waves from heavy DJ bass can cause strong vibrations in the body and chest and may interfere with the heart’s electrical system. This can lead to an abnormal heart rhythm, or arrhythmia, which in severe cases can result in sudden cardiac arrest. C. Silent heart blockage The copy explains that some people may have undetected narrowing or blockage in the arteries supplying blood to the heart. A sudden rise in blood pressure and stress may contribute to plaque rupture and clot formation, potentially blocking blood flow to the heart and causing a heart attack. D. Greater risk for people with heart conditions People with existing high blood pressure or heart disease may be more vulnerable to the effects of intense noise, especially when combined with factors such as heat, crowds and physical stress. Question 2: Did loud noise cause the girl’s death in Balrampur? Answer: The exact cause has not been established. According to the copy, the incident occurred on September 21 and the police were informed only after a video surfaced on September 22. The girl had already been cremated, so no post-mortem was conducted. Doctors cited in the copy have suggested that the extremely loud DJ sound could have triggered a severe cardiovascular response. However, this remains an inference rather than a confirmed cause of death. The copy also notes that children can have previously undiagnosed congenital heart conditions, which could make an individual more vulnerable to a sudden cardiac event. Question 3: What are the rules for DJs and sound systems in Uttar Pradesh? The copy says that loudspeakers and DJs are regulated under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. It states that: Written administrative permission is required for using DJs or loudspeakers at public or religious places. Use of loudspeakers, DJs and amplifiers in the open is prohibited between 10pm and 6am, subject to the stated exceptions. The Balrampur police are investigating whether the rules were followed during the procession and are also examining the DJ equipment used. Question 4: How can you measure the noise level at a location? Noise intensity can be measured using a decibel meter. The copy mentions mobile apps such as Decibel X, SPL Meter and Sound Meter Noise Detector for approximate measurements.

stories.title: ‘Food is so bad even dogs won’t eat it’:PAC jawan shares pain; venomous snakes enter beds, they clean toilets themselves; where does budget go?
stories.summary: PAC personnel posted in Barabanki have alleged that poor barracks, bad food, lack of leave, inadequate drinking water and power cuts during extreme heat are among the common problems they face, with constable Devendra Gupta saying they are sometimes made to stay in places “where even animals would not stay”. Gupta, posted with a PAC battalion in Barabanki, said, “We are given food that even a dog would not eat. We even have to clean the toilets ourselves,” and claimed that PAC personnel cannot speak openly about these conditions. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Devendra to understand the alleged lack of basic facilities in the PAC. Constable claims: ‘We are being kept in places like cattle sheds’ There are nine PAC companies in Barabanki, with around 1,100 personnel posted there. Devendra Gupta is also posted there. Devendra says PAC personnel remain posted at police headquarters for only one or two months a year. For the remaining nine to 10 months, they are sent to different districts for duty. “There are no proper arrangements for accommodation at the places where we are sent. If you go and see these places, you will be shocked and wonder how any human being can stay there. The conditions are like a buffalo shed,” he says. He claims PAC personnel are housed in some of the city’s most dilapidated and poorly maintained buildings. “Mosquitoes bite us during the day. Poisonous snakes come onto our beds, while rats, cats and monkeys enter the rooms. There is no security for our lives or our belongings. What are we? Machines or animals?” he asks. ‘Not a single constable is happy, everyone is silent for fear of suspension’ We asked Devendra whether he was afraid of disciplinary action after making videos about his problems. “It is true that anyone who raises their voice will either be suspended by the officers or asked to give an explanation. Because of this fear, no constable speaks up. But the reality is that not a single constable in the department is happy,” he says. He alleges that when officers come for inspections, they check the constables’ uniforms and belts. “If they find even a minor deficiency, disciplinary action is immediately taken. But no officer checks the hell in which the constable is living. This is affecting the mental well-being of the personnel,” he says. Devendra also questioned the sanitation arrangements. “There must be a budget for phenyl and cleaning materials to clean the toilets and barracks. Then where does that money go?” he asks. ‘I was not given paternity leave after becoming a father’ Devendra had not mentioned leave in his video, but after controversy grew around his post, the PAC Barabanki issued an official response. The department said Devendra had already taken 25 days of earned leave (EL) and 19 days of casual leave (CL) this year. Devendra says his wife was pregnant and gave birth this month, which is why he had to take 25 days of earned leave. “Under the rules, the department provides 15 days of paternity leave when a personnel becomes a father. I applied for it on September 15, but the officers rejected my application. “If my leave appears excessive this year, the officers should look at my service record for the past three years. I have taken only a nominal amount of leave during that period,” he says. ‘Everything is fine in paperwork, but constables are suffering on the ground’ PAC Barabanki, in its response, said welfare meetings are held every month to resolve the problems faced by personnel. It said issues are discussed with officers and resolved. Devendra disputes this. “A meeting is held every month, but only the battalion in-charge, such as the subedar or in-charge officer, attends it. They simply tell the senior officers that everything is fine. They can see the problems on the ground, but they do not have the courage to speak about them in front of senior officers,” he says. PAC constable makes VIDEO and seeks justice from Chief Minister On September 22, Devendra Gupta shared a 6-minute-42-second video. For the first 5 minutes and 48 seconds, he spoke about his own difficulties and those of his colleagues. In the final 1 minute and 8 seconds, he included an episode from the Mahabharata in which Lord Krishna appears before Dhritarashtra’s court seeking justice. Devendra, who is from the Gorakhpur region, appealed to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, saying: Chief Minister, I come from your own parliamentary constituency. You have listened to the grievances of lakhs of helpless and poor people in the state and worked for their welfare. Now we hope that you will also listen to the pain of us constables. PAC personnel perform duty round the clock in scorching heat, severe cold and torrential rain. Please bring reforms to this corrupt and dilapidated system and impose strict rules against officers who harass constables over every little issue. Hundreds of comments have appeared on Devendra Gupta’s video from UP Police and PAC personnel, who are describing the poor conditions in their own barracks and alleging problems with the attitude of officers.

stories.title: Azamgarh case:5-year-old searches for parents, brother, asks crying, ‘I want to play with Shaurya’; all three cremated on one pyre
stories.summary: The accused who allegedly killed his wife, son and two priests in Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh was shot dead in an encounter, leaving the family’s two young daughters searching for their mother, father and brother. The five-year-old girl still does not understand that her parents and brother will never return; her maternal uncle is looking after her, but she repeatedly breaks down while remembering them. She asks, “Where is brother Shaurya? I want to play with him.” There is no one to answer her questions. The seven-month-old girl, meanwhile, is still too young to understand that her parents and brother have been separated from her forever. The two daughters from the same family are experiencing the tragedy in their own ways. One is searching for her loved ones, while the other is not yet old enough to understand what she has lost. This is the story of a family torn apart… First, know the full case At around 6 pm on Tuesday, Arvind Singh (42), from Shambhupur village under Ahiraula police station, around 50 km from the Azamgarh district headquarters, allegedly shot dead his wife Babita, son Shaurya (9), and priests Mahendra Pathak (60) and Akhilesh Mishra (55). The family is now left with Arvind’s mother Kamla Devi (70) and his two daughters, Pari (5) and Shambhavi (7 months). Fearing arrest, Arvind Singh held his three children hostage inside a room. Seven hours later, he fired at his son. ATS and SOG teams subsequently killed Arvind Singh. According to police, the family suspected that Arvind was being troubled by the spirit of his brother Sunil. His wife and mother had therefore arranged a Mahamrityunjaya chant. Arvind was angry about this. At around 6 pm on Tuesday, he argued with his wife over the issue. He allegedly said, “Your brother was killed because of you. Now you are creating a drama here.” He then asked the priests for their Aadhaar cards and got into an argument with them. In the middle of this, he brought a licensed revolver from the room and allegedly shot his wife and the two priests. At around 7 pm on Wednesday, Arvind Singh, his wife Babita and son Shaurya Singh were cremated together on a single pyre. Arvind’s niece Varsha lit the funeral pyre. Husband, wife and son cremated on the same pyre Arvind Singh, his wife Babita and son Shaurya were cremated together at Rajghat in Azamgarh at around 7 pm on Wednesday. Priest Mahendra Pathak was cremated near Durvasa Dham in Phulpur, while priest Akhilesh Mishra was cremated at Kamariya Ghat in Ambedkar Nagar district. Arvind Singh’s firing also injured his five-year-old daughter Pari. The bullet grazed her hand, causing minor injuries. She is undergoing treatment at the district hospital and remains shaken after the incident. Nine-hour postmortem: eight bullets hit five people The postmortem examinations of all five bodies took around nine hours on Wednesday. A team comprising Additional CMO Dr Alendra Kumar, Dr HL Saroj and Dr Sanjay Gaur conducted the postmortems under video recording. The bullet injuries caused severe damage to the victims’ heads. Priest Akhilesh Mishra’s postmortem was conducted at around 10.30 am on Wednesday. He had been hit by two bullets in the head. Priest Mahendra Pathak’s postmortem was conducted at around 11.15 am. One bullet was lodged in his head. The postmortems of Babita and Shaurya were completed at around 1.30 pm. One bullet passed through Shaurya’s head, while one bullet was lodged in Babita’s head. Arvind Singh’s postmortem was completed last, at around 7 pm. He was killed during the commando operation. He had been hit by three bullets, two in the chest and one on the lower right side of his abdomen. No one came forward to prepare the accused’s panchnama The bodies of the husband, wife and son were lying at the postmortem house, but no one from the village came forward to prepare the panchnama for Arvind Singh until afternoon. Women from Babita’s maternal family arrived and helped prepare the panchnamas for Babita and Shaurya. Their postmortems were conducted afterwards. Babita’s maternal family, however, refused to help prepare the panchnama for Arvind Singh. The police then brought Arvind Singh’s mother, sister and niece from the village. The postmortem proceedings began at around 4 pm, after which his body was examined. Brother was killed eight years ago, had been Balasaheb Thackeray’s gunman In 2018, Arvind’s brother Sunil Singh was allegedly shot dead by his cousins. Sunil lived in Maharashtra and had worked as Balasaheb Thackeray’s gunman. Suraj Singh, the brother of Sunil’s wife, said, “My brother-in-law had gone to the village with Arvind to attend a bhandara. At that point, his cousins Manish Singh and Avnish surrounded them. They chased Sunil and shot him. They also assaulted Arvind.” Suraj said, “After the incident, my sister Mamta, Sunil’s wife, lodged a named complaint against Manish and Avnish. The police arrested both of them and sent them to jail. They were released from jail only about one-and-a-half months ago.” He further alleged, “Babita was having an affair with Manish. My brother-in-law Sunil had found out about it. He had lodged complaints against Manish in several cases, including theft, snatching and molestation. Manish killed Sunil because of this rivalry.” Eyewitness priest says: ‘First the wife, then both priests were shot’ Pandit Himanshu told police that Arvind was believed to be troubled by the spirit of his elder brother Sunil Singh. Arvind’s mother Kamla Devi and wife Babita had therefore called the priests to conduct a puja. Himanshu said, “The puja had been going on for four days. The Purnahuti was scheduled for Tuesday. Four of us, including me, my father Akhilesh Mishra and Pandit Mahendra Pathak, were conducting the puja." “On Monday, Arvind had warned us not to come the next day. He was opposed to the puja.“ At around 6 pm on Tuesday, he returned from the market and started arguing with his wife. When we went to intervene, he began abusing us. He asked us for our Aadhaar cards. “We told him, ‘We are priests. Why would we carry Aadhaar cards around? We are neither hawkers nor have we come from Nepal or Bangladesh.’ But he remained adamant." Meanwhile, Babita said, ‘Do not insult the priests.’ Arvind then said, ‘Your brother was killed because of you. Now you are creating a drama here.’ After this, he shot his wife Babita. “When we tried to run away, he shot my father. The other priest, Mahendra, had reached the doorway when Arvind shot him as well. I jumped over a wall to save my life. His mother also ran outside. People gathered after hearing the sound of gunfire. Seeing this, Arvind locked himself inside a room with his three children. The police arrived after neighbours informed them.”

stories.title: Millionaire businessman murder:Servant says son, not daughter-in-law, ordered killing; Shalu cried seeing husband, Kanpur cops asked 40 questions
stories.summary: Police on Wednesday confronted accused daughter-in-law Shalu, domestic help Vishal and son Subrat in the murder case of Kanpur millionaire drug trader Vineet Minocha. Police Commissioner Raghuveer Lal questioned the three accused in several rounds at the Police Lines. During questioning, domestic help Vishal alleged that he killed Vineet on Subrat’s instructions. He claimed Subrat had promised to pay him Rs 6 lakh and told him to name Shalu if he was caught. Vishal also said that he had stolen medicines from the shop on Subrat’s instructions. According to him, Vineet had scolded Subrat after the theft was discovered, leading to an argument between the two. Vishal was subsequently dismissed from his job. According to police, Shalu broke down after seeing her husband Subrat during questioning and said, “You have framed me.” Vineet Minocha was murdered inside his apartment on the night of September 5. Domestic help Vishal and his associate Rajkishore allegedly stabbed him 26 times. When police arrested the two, Vishal named Vineet’s daughter-in-law Shalu. All three accused are currently in jail, while police are also questioning Shalu’s husband Subrat. What emerged during police custody remand ‘Brother had said: Kill him in a way that makes it look like a natural death’ During questioning, domestic help Vishal claimed that before the murder, Subrat had called him and told him that the incident should be carried out in such a way that it looked like a natural death rather than murder. According to Vishal, Subrat called him six times on the day of the murder and repeatedly spoke in a hurry. Vishal said Vineet Minocha saw the two men inside the room and began raising an alarm. He claimed that he attacked Vineet with a knife out of fear. Police then questioned Subrat, who rejected Vishal’s allegations. Subrat said, “I do not know why Vishal is making such statements. I never asked Vishal to steal.” Shalu broke down after seeing her husband Police then questioned Subrat and his wife Shalu face-to-face. According to police, Shalu became emotional and started crying as soon as she saw Subrat. The questioning continued, while Subrat did not respond emotionally to her. Shalu kept crying, Subrat did not even look at her During questioning, Shalu cried in front of the officers and said that Subrat knew her well, yet he had not even come to meet her in jail. Police officers calmed her down before continuing the questioning. Shalu maintained her earlier statements and denied having arranged the murder of her father-in-law, Vineet Minocha. According to her, she had a good relationship with Vineet and also took full care of his diet because he was diabetic. When police asked why Vishal had named her, Shalu said she herself was shocked and did not know at whose behest Vishal had taken her name. When police told her that Vishal had said in his statement that Subrat had instructed him to name her, Shalu looked at both Subrat and Vishal for some time. Throughout this, Shalu kept looking towards Subrat, while he did not look at her. Shalu told Subrat: ‘You framed me’ Shalu confronted her husband Subrat after 18 days during police custody remand. During around an hour of questioning, Shalu repeatedly looked at Subrat. She had questions about why her husband had not come to meet her in jail and why Vishal had accused her of being involved in the murder conspiracy. Meanwhile, Subrat continued to avoid looking at her. When Subrat accused Shalu of being involved in his father’s murder, she broke down and said, “You framed me to save yourself.” Shalu cried three to four times during the questioning. She told officers that she had trusted Subrat deeply but that her trust in him had now been broken. More than 40 questions, with every second recorded on video Police officers prepared a list of more than 40 questions as part of the murder investigation. The investigation is being led by a joint team comprising Police Commissioner Raghuveer Lal, DCP West SM Qasim Abidi, an inspector and three sub-inspectors. The entire investigation was videographed. The accused’ facial expressions, changes in their speech while allegedly lying and every admission made during questioning were recorded on camera so that they could not later retract their statements before the court. Key found near Ratan Orbit boundary On Wednesday, police took Vishal to Ratan Orbit in Kalyanpur’s Keshavpuram. According to police, Vishal had thrown a key there while fleeing after jumping over the boundary wall of Ratan Orbit. Police said the key was recovered from an empty plot adjoining the boundary wall. Meanwhile, another accused, Rajkishore, was taken to Central Station. On his identification, police recovered his blood-stained trousers and a black scarf from behind a public toilet. Subrat and Shalu did not recognise Rajkishore According to police, Rajkishore was also confronted with Subrat and Shalu, but both sides denied recognising each other. During questioning, Rajkishore told police that he had committed the crime at Vishal’s request. He said he carried out the crime because he needed money and had never met Shalu or Subrat before. Main questions asked to Subrat and his answers Police: What was your relationship with your father? Subrat: My father was good and caring. He handled all the responsibilities of the family. Police: What was the relationship between your parents? Subrat: They had a good relationship. My mother Punita stayed in Kanpur for a few months and in Delhi for a few months. We also have a flat in Delhi. Police: What was your relationship with your wife? Subrat: Our relationship was good. There were disagreements over some family matters, which is normal. Police: What happened when goods went missing from the shop on Birhana Road? Subrat: A carton of Electral went missing from the shop. I had it removed with Vishal’s help. My father scolded me in front of everyone at the shop. There was also an argument at home. Police: You had gone to Dehradun after being called by a medicine company. What happened there? Subrat: A bag went missing from the hotel. It contained several important documents. My father scolded me severely over it. Police: Do you have a female friend in Canada whom you met in Dehradun? Subrat: Yes, I have a friend. But we are only friends. Police: Vishal is now naming you. Did you have your father killed? Subrat: Vishal initially named Shalu. Now he is trying to frame me. Police: Your father had dismissed Vishal over allegations of theft and did not like him. Why did you remain in contact with him? Subrat: He helped me with various small and big tasks. In return, I helped him financially. Police: You always needed money. Did your father give you less money? Subrat: It is true that my father gave me limited money. Our lifestyle was high, so the money always fell short. Police: Even after receiving Rs 40,000 a month, you attended expensive parties and kitty parties? Subrat: I used credit cards and took help from friends. This is why I also got into debt. Police: Did you plan your father’s murder because of your debt and frame Shalu? Subrat: No, absolutely not. I could not have my father killed for money. Police: Why did you not recognise Vishal even after seeing him in the CCTV footage on the day of the murder? Subrat: I had drunk a lot of alcohol at the party, so I could not recognise him. Subrat has a debt of around Rs 15 lakh Police questioning has revealed that Subrat has debts of around Rs 15 lakh. During questioning, he said his debt had increased because of credit card expenses, parties and his interest in travelling. Police have also received information about him losing money through gaming and betting. Round-wise questioning after blood sugar rose According to sources, Subrat is diabetic. His blood sugar reportedly rose significantly during questioning on Wednesday. Sources claimed that at one point his blood sugar level went above 700. Considering his health, police are questioning him in multiple rounds.

stories.summary: UP Assembly Election 2027: AIMIM के मुखिया असदुद्दीन ओवैसी ने उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा चुनाव को लेकर बड़ी बात कही है। न्यूज एजेंसी ANI से बातचीत के दौरान उन्होंने कहा- ‘यूपी असेंबली इलेक्शन नजदीक है। लेकिन यह 2014 का इलेक्शन नहीं होगा, न ही 2017, न 2019 का इलेक्शन, न 2022 का इलेक्शन। यह बिल्कुल अलग इलेक्शन होने वाला है। और बहुत चैलेंजिंग भी होगा क्योंकि BJP ने अपने किए वादे पूरे नहीं किए हैं। जब समाजवादी पार्टी पावर में थी, तो Y नॉर्म था। अब, T यहां नॉर्म है, और उससे आगे, गवर्नेंस गुड गवर्नेंस नहीं है। आपके (BJP) कानून राज में कई गरीब लोगों की जमीन छीन ली गई है। इसलिए, डेवलपमेंट के बहुत सारे इश्यू हैं। बिजली बहुत बड़ा इश्यू है। कोई फर्क नहीं है। पहले जो होता था वह यह था कि समाजवादी पार्टी की सरकार में एक अलग तरह की गुंडागर्दी होती थी। कोई और करता था। अब इनके सरकार में एक अलग तरह की गुंडागर्दी हो रही है। यह किसी के लिए भी आसान इलेक्शन नहीं होगा। यह होने वाला है। उत्तर प्रदेश में एक अलग चुनाव…SIT रिपोर्ट (राम मंदिर गबन मामले की) जनता के सामने क्यों नहीं आती? सरकार इसे क्यों नहीं जारी करती? और उन लोगों को बेल क्यों मिल रही है? उन्हें बेल कैसे मिल रही है? यह अजीब है। यह भी एक बड़ा मुद्दा होगा।’

stories.title: UP transfers 10 IAS officers:Amit Kumar Ghosh appointed additional chief secretary for higher education
stories.summary: The state government transferred 10 senior IAS officers on Sunday night. Following the displeasure expressed by Panchayati Raj Minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) president Om Prakash Rajbhar, Anil Kumar was removed as the department's principal secretary and appointed principal secretary of the Food and Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Department. Meanwhile, Ashish Goyal, Additional Chief Secretary of the Energy Department and chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation, was removed and appointed Additional Chief Secretary of the Labour and Employment Department. Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma had not been getting along with Ashish Goyal over the power crisis that had continued in the state from the summer through the monsoon. At a meeting recently, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath reprimanded Ashish Goyal over the issue of power theft. The Chief Minister was also unhappy with his working style. Amrit Abhijat, a close associate and batchmate of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's Additional Chief Secretary Sanjay Prasad, has once again been given greater authority. Along with the charge of Additional Chief Secretary of the Tourism and Culture Department, he has also been given the charge of Additional Chief Secretary of the Transport Department. Meanwhile, relations between Higher Education Department Principal Secretary Mahendra Kumar Agrawal and his minister, Yogendra Upadhyay, had deteriorated over delays in scooter distribution and laxity in departmental functioning. The Chief Minister was also not very pleased. Therefore, Mahendra Kumar Agrawal has been removed from the Higher Education Department and appointed Principal Secretary of the Forest and Environment Department. Medical and Health Department Additional Chief Secretary Amit Ghosh has been transferred again, three and a half months before his retirement. He has been appointed Additional Chief Secretary of the Higher Education Department. See the list 10 IAS Transfers

stories.title: 60-65-year-old men became Class 6 students:Played gilli-danda at school; relived their childhood
stories.summary: Former students aged 60-65 returned to Agra's Government Inter College wearing Class 6 uniforms. Dressed in white shirts, black trousers and water bottles hanging around their necks, the friends relived their childhood days. While some ran through the school gate, others sat in the classroom and played pranks. These friends are retired IPS officers, doctors, accountants and teachers. The college's former students made the video around seven years ago to relive their school days. Rakesh, who shot the video, said, "Some parts of the video were uploaded on Instagram on Friday with a new voice-over. Since then, large numbers of people have been viewing and sharing it." Video made 7 years ago Rakesh, who lives in Raja Mandi Gokulpura, says the friends made this video around seven years ago, in 2019, for their YouTube channel, 'Bhoot Ka Anda'. The video received around 1,500 views at the time. Four days ago, parts of the video were reposted on Instagram with a new voice-over. Since then, large numbers of people have been watching and sharing it. The video shows the elderly friends, aged 60-65, entering the school through the gate wearing white shirts, black trousers, and water bottles hanging around their necks. All the friends played childhood games The video shows some friends running into their classroom, while others arrive dancing with their friends. They then appear playing childhood games on the school grounds. They play pitthu, also known as seven stones, and gilli-danda. The excitement on their faces while playing is the same as it was in their childhood. The video also shows the friends visiting the school corridors and classrooms and sitting on the benches. At times, they are seen having fun while holding each other's hands, and at other times, they form a train and run around the classroom. Some friends are also seen dancing to songs. The voice-over playing in the background talks about a friendship spanning nearly 50 years, childhood memories, and staying connected with friends. Now read how the group of friends was formed and where the idea for the video came from.... The group of friends was formed 10 years ago Rakesh Nagar said that about 10 years ago, his friend Keshav Sharma had created a WhatsApp group of former classmates. Gradually, other school friends also joined the group. It includes doctors, chartered accountants, bank and BSNL employees, businesspeople, and others who have worked in different fields. Rakesh said, "One day, I sent a script to the group for making a video about our old school memories." All the friends liked the idea. After this, preparations began to shoot at the school to relive their Class 6 days. After the teacher explained, they were allowed to shoot Rakesh said, "Initially, we were not allowed to shoot at the school. After that, teacher Dr Janak Singh Sisodia explained the entire matter to the principal. The shoot could take place after permission was granted. Dr Sisodia also appeared in the video with the friends." Rakesh said, "The video was shot at Government Inter College. Around 30 friends reached the school dressed like sixth-grade students. Some entered through the school gate, while others were seen sitting in classrooms and misbehaving as they had in the old days." He said that several of the friends featured in the video are now retired IPS officers, doctors, accountants and teachers. Some friends could not take part in the shoot. They included a DGP, an IPS officer, and Dr Arun, a neurosurgeon. Dr Arun joined his friends via video call. He said their group of friends is not limited to school memories. The friends organise an event every year. They also stand by one another during weddings and on occasions of happiness and grief. Enrolled at this school in 1971 Rakesh said, "I enrolled in Class Six at Government Inter College in 1971. I passed Class Ten in 1976. During my school days, I acted on stage and took part in programmes. After school, I worked in private jobs, at a bank and a private school. Since I had a good voice, people advised me to take up singing. I have been singing for several years now. I have a group called 'Karan Priya Music Event'. I have also written a book."

stories.title: Men posing as police officers kidnap businessman in Lucknow:They beat him while driving him to Agra and Kannauj, extort ₹13 lakh ransom
stories.summary: In Lucknow, six young men posing as police officers kidnapped an antique dealer. They held him hostage in a Scorpio and beat him at gunpoint. They forced him to call his wife and demand 15 lakh rupees, threatening to kill him if the money was not sent. On Sunday, eight days after the incident, the police arrested the six accused. Four of them are residents of Bulandshahr in UP, while two are from Bihar. The plot to kidnap the businessman was hatched in Patna, with one of the businessman's own partners involved. He had conducted reconnaissance around seven times over 20 days. Fake ID cards for an inspector, sub-inspector, and constables were recovered from the accused. They had made the businessman get into the Scorpio under the pretext of questioning him after showing him these fake ID cards. Now Read in Detail… Lucknow South DCP Mohammad Mushtaq stated that Sudarshan Ghosh lives in Saket Apartments in Rajendranagar, Alambagh. On 13 September, he lodged a complaint at the Krishnanagar police station. Sudarshan explained that he runs a large antique shop in Alambagh. On 12 September, while heading to his shop, several individuals posing as police officers forcibly bundled him into a vehicle. They intimidated him with weapons and beat him when he resisted. The hardened criminals kept him hostage in the vehicle for nearly nine hours, driving him along the routes between Lucknow, Agra, and Kannauj. They continuously issued death threats while demanding a ransom. Eventually, the businessman called his wife and asked her to bring the ransom amount to a location specified by the accused. The wife dispatched ₹13 lakh and some jewellery through their driver. The accused collected the ransom in Kannauj before abandoning the businessman on Shaheed Path and fleeing. Upon returning home, Sudarshan Ghosh recounted the entire ordeal to his family and lodged a case at the police station the following day. One Accused Was Close to the Businessman; He Gave the Signal for the Abduction During interrogation, the accused told the police that they committed robberies as a gang. The gang consists of people from different states. They used to target individuals who had a significant amount of money. Following this, they would conduct reconnaissance before executing the crime. According to the police, one of the youths involved in robbing the Lucknow businessman is from Patna. He is close to the businessman. He provided information regarding the businessman's financial status and movements to his accomplices. After this, they all stayed in Lucknow and carried out reconnaissance on the businessman. 3 Key Points— Asserted dominance using police ID cards: 4 police ID cards were recovered from the accused. They used to intimidate people using these very cards. The gang possesses several other vehicles: During questioning, the accused revealed that the Scorpio was not their only vehicle. The gang has several other vehicles. They used fake number plates on the vehicles to prevent the police from identifying them. After the crime, all the accused had scattered to different states. They had already divided the cash and jewellery obtained in Lucknow among themselves. Returned to Lucknow for another crime: The accused had returned to Lucknow to carry out their next crime. It was during this time that the police arrested them. Police action is ongoing regarding the role of other accused in the case and the recovery of the remaining jewellery and cash received as ransom. Scrutinised Over 220 CCTV Footages Eight police teams were formed to solve the case. The Surveillance Cell of the Southern Zone was also deployed for the investigation. Using roughly 220 to 240 CCTV footages, technical evidence, manual inputs, and the local intelligence network, the police teams identified the accused. The police have arrested six accused in the case. These include Anurag (26), Lavi Kumar (30), Deepanshu Kumar (24), and Akash Chaudhary (23), all residents of Shikarpur in Bulandshahr. Anurag Kumar (33), a resident of Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and Manish Kumar (24), a resident of Sonepur in Saran district, have also been arrested.

stories.title: Congress protests reduction in reservation at UP medical colleges:Rajendra Gautam says govt failed to present its case in court; gives 24-hour ultimatum
stories.summary: UP Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has held the present government responsible for the stay on the SC-ST reservation implemented in four government medical colleges in the state. He said that due to the government's laxity and weak representation in the High Court, the rights of students from the Dalit community are being infringed upon. He has warned the government to clarify its position on the entire matter within 24 hours. Rajendra Pal Gautam claimed that there were a total of 200 seats in the medical colleges of Ambedkar Nagar, Kannौज, Jalaun, and Saharanpur. The construction and operation of these four colleges were not funded by the general budget, but by funds from the 'Special Component Plan' (SCP) earmarked for Scheduled Castes. Since the money came from the Dalit Welfare Fund, 70% of the seats were reserved for students from the SC-ST category under the rules. Gautam alleged that during the hearing in the High Court, instead of advocating for the 70% reservation, the government's lawyer spoke only of the standard 21% reservation. ‘How Did the Verdict Come Without Hearing the Affected Students?’ The Congress leader raised questions about the High Court’s procedure and the government’s lukewarm attitude. He said that the students whose futures were set to be impacted by this decision were not even given a hearing in court. The matter is currently pending before the Division Bench of the High Court. According to Gautam, the government must immediately take legal steps and demand a stay on the Single Bench’s order. Allegation of Irregularities in Scholarship and Fee Funds Gautam also raised the issue of irregularities in the scholarship and fee money for Dalit students. He said that earlier, the fees of SC students taking admission to professional and higher education were directly sent to the institutions through the government system. Now, students are forced to pay the full fee out of their own pockets first, after which the process for scholarships and fee reimbursement begins. As a result, students from poor families are unable to pay the fees and are forced to drop out midway. The Congress has announced a state-wide agitation regarding this issue. ‘Comments on Rahul Gandhi’s Mother Are Inappropriate’ He expressed displeasure over the statements made by BJP leaders regarding Rahul Gandhi’s mother, Sonia Gandhi. Gautam said that families of leaders, especially mothers, should not be dragged into political battles. Regarding the party’s election strategy, he said that the state president and the in-charge will tour different regions. Six AICC (All India Congress Committee) secretaries have been assigned responsibility for different areas so that the entire state can be covered in a short period.

Despite attempts to vitiate the atmosphere, the party is grateful to our Muslim brothers for the patience, brotherhood, and goodwill they displayed.” Not Even 10% PDA Representation Among Election Officials Akhilesh Yadav raised questions about the administrative preparations for the elections as well. stories.title: SP leaders clash in Akhilesh's presence:Party chief says they have grown arrogant with money, expels them from meeting
stories.summary: Two Samajwadi Party leaders clashed in front of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. After a heated argument, they began hurling abuses at each other. Akhilesh became angry on seeing this and had both leaders, Manjeet Yadav and Jugendra Yadav, removed from the meeting. Akhilesh said angrily, "They are all senior leaders. Ask these people for advice. Go and do whatever you want to do. When a person keeps refusing to listen to the party and has poor conduct, who are we supposed to take it out on... tell me. It's all right, these things happen. It is all arrogance caused by money. Remember, whoever ends up with more money will leave you and go." After this, Akhilesh Yadav left the meeting. An hour later, the party units in both Etah and Kasganj districts were dissolved. The entire incident took place during a meeting at the SP office in Lucknow on Saturday. However, a video of it emerged today. Manjeet and Jugendra exchanged abuses during Samajwadi Party meeting Akhilesh had called the meeting to discuss the party's position in Etah and Kasganj districts and preparations for the Assembly elections. A total of 250 leaders and office-bearers from both districts were present. Akhilesh was seeking information from the leaders about the election preparations and the organisation. During the meeting, Samajwadi Party leader Manjeet Yadav, nephew of former Legislative Council chairman Ramesh Yadav, began speaking about the party's position in the previous elections and the reasons for its defeat. After this, former Etah district panchayat chairman Jugendra Singh Yadav stood up to speak. Manjeet Yadav objected to some of the words used by Jugendra Singh Yadav. A heated argument then broke out between the two. The leaders present at the meeting tried to defuse the situation, but neither of them calmed down. Before long, the two began hurling abuses at each other. This made the atmosphere at the meeting uncomfortable. Angry, Akhilesh Yadav told both leaders to maintain discipline, but neither of them complied. The SP chief then lost his temper.

stories.title: Father dies after hearing of son's death:He collapsed in Prayagraj, family splashed water on him but he did not get up
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, a 52-year-old father died after hearing that his son had passed away. The 28-year-old man was killed in a car collision at around 10:30 p.m. on Saturday. About an hour later, at 11:30 p.m., his daughter told her father, "My brother is no more." On hearing the news, the father clutched his chest and collapsed to the ground. Seeing this, the daughter screamed. The family splashed water on the father's face to revive him. When he did not regain consciousness, they took him to hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The doctors said he had suffered a heart attack. The incident took place in the area under Soraon police station, around 35 km from the district headquarters. Now read the full story... The son had gone to visit relatives and was returning at night Sister received the news of her brother's death The police reached the spot at around 11.00 pm. With the help of local people, they took Shivam to a private hospital in Prayagraj. Shivam died during treatment. At around 11.30 pm, the police took the mobile phone from Shivam's pocket and called his family. His sister Sunita answered the call. The police told her that Shivam had died in an accident. As soon as she heard the news of her brother's death, she began crying loudly. Weeping, she went to her father, who was sleeping outside the house. She told him that her brother was no more and had died in an accident. As soon as he heard this, Ram Singh also let out a loud cry. He suffered severe chest pain after hearing the news of his son's death Father Ram Singh got up from the charpoy, crying. As he stood up, he suffered severe chest pain and collapsed on the floor. His family tried to revive him. When he failed to regain consciousness, they took him to a private hospital in Shantipuram, where doctors declared him dead. Road blocked and protest staged Police searching for absconding driver Soron Station House Officer Deendayal Singh said the absconding driver was being traced based on the car's registration number. A case has been registered under the relevant sections based on the family's complaint. Police are taking further legal action in the matter.

stories.title: FIR against girls for abusing MP Chandrashekhar:Said, ‘Scared to come to Gonda? Mend your ways; abused you, will do it again… not afraid of cases’
stories.summary: FIR has been registered against two girls from Gonda for allegedly abusing MP Chandrashekhar Azad. They are accused of releasing a video containing abusive remarks after the MP's visit to Gonda was cancelled on 17 September. In the video, one of the girls says, "Why didn't you come to Gonda? Were you scared? Mend your ways. If you have the courage, come to Gonda and show it." They said, "We have hurled abuses and will continue to do so. Brahmins are always superior. They will always be called superior. I am Pallavi, and this is Kajal. She has four cases against her and I have 22 cases. What difference would one more FIR make? We are not afraid of cases." A video of Pallavi Shukla and Kajal Singh emerged on 18 September. Ramkishun Kohli, a former Bhim Army office-bearer, posted the video on social media that day and demanded police action. Following this, Sub-Inspector Yogendra Yadav registered a case at Kauria police station at around 11:30 pm on Saturday night. Kajal (30) and Pallavi (20) are both social media creators and live separately from their families. Five cases have been registered against Kajal. She is married but lived separately from her husband. Pallavi had previously commented on Chandrashekhar, and a case had also been registered against her. Now, understand the full case Chandrashekhar Azad was scheduled to visit Gonda on 17 September to meet the family of businessman Vinod Sahni, who was killed. However, he suddenly cancelled his visit. Earlier, on 13 September, he had also been travelling to Gonda, but the police turned him back from Barabanki. During this, Chandrashekhar's supporters and the police also jostled with each other. After his visit was cancelled on both occasions, Pallavi Shukla posted a video on 18 September. In it, she is seen with Kajal. Kajal says that neither of them is afraid of the case, nor will they ever be. She says, "You already know about our influence. Chandrashekhar Azad Ravana was coming to Gonda district, but he did not come. Did he get scared? Chandrashekhar Ravana, mend your ways. We oppose you. You have shown great bravado; you will get one more case registered-what else will you do? Chandrashekhar, when are you coming? Did you get scared after hearing the name of Gonda district?" stories.title: Mayawati will not hand over BSP to niece:Says, 'She may change after marriage just like Akash, will promote Ishan'
stories.summary: BSP chief Mayawati has said that her niece Deepika Anand will also not be given any responsibility in the party, while her nephew Akash Anand’s younger brother, Ishan, will be promoted within the organisation. In a post on X on Sunday, Mayawati said Akash had come completely under the influence of his father-in-law, Ashok Siddharth. She said bringing him back into the party would amount to a “major betrayal” of the organisation and that she would not make such a mistake. Mayawati said, If the issue concerning my niece after her marriage also turns out to be similar to that of Akash Anand, it will not be in the party’s interest. Therefore, both will be kept away from party responsibilities. There will be no change in this decision. Instead, only Ishan from Anand Kumar’s family will now be given responsibility in the party and promoted. Seven days earlier, Mayawati had indicated that her niece Deepika Anand could be given responsibility in the party. She had said that if her brother Anand Kumar needed help from a family member, he could seek assistance from his only daughter, Deepika. She had also said that Deepika could be given a party responsibility in future based on her honesty and capabilities. Deepika, 19, is currently studying law. Read Mayawati's four major points 1- Akash was brought to the fore at Anand Kumar's request Mayawati said that she had to promote Anand Kumar's elder son, Akash Anand, in politics at Anand Kumar's special request. After his marriage, Akash Anand's conduct and activities were such that he had to be removed from the party a few days ago. In such a situation, deciding whether or not to promote someone from Anand Kumar's family in the party had been a dilemma for her for some time. 2- If Ishan does not work properly, he will be expelled from the party The BSP supremo said that she had decided to promote a member of Anand's family who would not follow Akash's path at all. In such a situation, Ishan Anand would be promoted by being given a respectable responsibility in the party. For now, it appeared that he would have no association with anti-party activities, like Akash Anand and his sister. However, it could not yet be said what would happen in the future. If he too committed any serious anti-party act, he would also be expelled from the party. In such a situation, no other member of Anand Kumar's family would be given any responsibility, big or small, in the party. Instead, a dedicated and loyal worker from the Dalit community working in the party will be promoted. An all-India meeting has been called on 23 September to discuss this particular issue and other important matters related to the national and public interest. 3- The entire Bahujan community is my real family I want to say this about myself: the entire Bahujan community is my real family. My mission and vow are to use the master key to power to transform the Bahujan community from an oppressed class into the ruling class and ensure its welfare. For this, I can go to any extent, even against my brothers and sisters and other members of my family. 4- Party members must rise above their attachment to siblings and relatives I want to tell party members that if they want to succeed in politics and do something for society, they must, like me, rise above their attachment to their siblings and close relatives and work with honesty and dedication. That is why, after entering politics, BSP founder Kanshi Ram always kept away from giving political benefits to his close relatives. He allowed them to work in the party organisation only in a selfless capacity. Not only that, he devoted his entire life to the interests and welfare of the Bahujan Samaj instead of building a family of his own. Inspired by him, I too decided to follow his path. I devoted my entire life to the Bahujan Samaj. However, because I am a woman, circumstances forced me to always keep one of my siblings with me. For this reason, my younger brother Anand Kumar has been working in my service for the past several years. Mayawati cited Babasaheb's 1956 letter Babasaheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar had also set an example of this. On 23 February 1956, he wrote a letter from Delhi to his son, Yashwant B. Ambedkar. In it, he said that he had received several letters stating that Yashwant was not allowing Upsham to work as an accountant and cashier at the Buddhist Bhushan Printing Press. You think that by doing this, you will take control of the press. I am clearly warning you that this press is public property. It belongs neither to you nor to me. No irregularity in the accounting of public property can be permitted in any way. Your conduct has not been appropriate. If you do not follow my final instruction, I will remove you from the press. If you still disregard my warning, I will also initiate legal proceedings against you.

stories.summary: Around 11am on Sunday, the body of a man aged around 40 was found in an open drain near Madarsa Chauraha in the Rajghat police station area of Gorakhpur, triggering panic in the surrounding area. A crowd gathered at the spot after learning that a body was lying in the drain. Local residents informed the police. People living nearby accused the Municipal Corporation of negligence. They said the incident occurred because the drain had no slab covering it. Police had the body removed from the drain After receiving the information, Rajghat police reached the spot and had the body removed from the drain. Police personnel tried to have local residents identify the deceased. However, despite considerable efforts, the man could not be identified. Police took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. People raise questions over the lack of a slab over the drain Local residents said the deceased may have been intoxicated and could have fallen into the open drain at the time. However, this has not been officially confirmed. People also accused the Municipal Corporation of negligence for leaving the drain open. They said that if there had been a slab over the drain, the man would not have fallen into it and his life could have been saved. Cause of death remains unclear According to police, the deceased was around 40 years old. His identity has not yet been established, and it is also not known how he died. Police have begun investigating the case. The exact cause of death is expected to become clear after the post-mortem report is received. Open drains have claimed lives before too Accidents have occurred in the city before because of open drains. In August 2025, eight-year-old Afreen fell into an open drain under construction during the rains in the Ghoshipurwa area. She was swept away by the strong water current in the drain and died. Following the accident, questions were raised about the open drain and the safety arrangements during construction work. Meanwhile, in June, around 40-year-old Teter Das fell into an open drain near Bansmandi on Fatima Road. He died after falling into the drain.

stories.title: Protesters take out rally with 200 tractors against UGC:Yamuna Expressway blocked in Agra, clash with police; bulldozers deployed to stop them
stories.summary: The protest against the University Grants Commission's (UGC) new rules intensified again in Agra on Sunday morning. Protesters determined to march to the district collectorate pushed ahead despite police restrictions and blocked the Agra-Noida Yamuna Expressway. Police tried to stop the protesters at several points by placing JCB machines in the middle of the road, but the protesters moved past them. Clashes also broke out between the protesters and police during the confrontation. The UGC Mukti Morcha had already warned that it would gherao the district headquarters on 20 September. A day before the planned protest, protesters began a sit-in at Mudi Chauraha late on Saturday evening, 19 September. They remained at the site until late at night. The situation became tense again near Mudi Chauraha in the Khandoli police station area on Sunday morning. Police personnel have been deployed at the spot and the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) has also been called in. The protesters set off for the collectorate with around 200 tractors. Police tried to stop them by placing JCB machines and hydras in the middle of the road, but the protesters broke through the police cordon and continued towards the collectorate. They then reached the Agra-Yamuna-Noida Expressway, where they parked their vehicles across the road and blocked traffic. Police are trying to clear the road, while the protesters continue raising slogans. See 5 pictures- Three major protests in Agra against the UGC so far 1 September- Under the banner of the Kshatriya Sabha, people who reached Etmadpur tehsil with a motorcycle rally to submit a memorandum clashed with police before moving to the national highway in Etmadpur and blocking it. The protesters sat on a dharna, accusing the police of lathi-charging them and demanding the suspension of the officers involved. A confrontation with police followed, along with protests and a commotion. The sub-inspector accused in the incident was later suspended. 18 September- The Savarn Samaj and System Improvement Organisation organised a tractor march from Etmadpur to the collectorate. Police had already put up barricades in villages from the morning and stopped tractors from leaving the villages. Despite this, hundreds of people reached the Agra-Kanpur Highway. They clashed with police, leading to a traffic blockade on the highway. Around 20 tractors took part in the protest. After nearly five hours of tension, the police and administration arranged a conversation with the Deputy Chief Minister. The protesters were assured that their demands would be conveyed to a Union minister. 20 September- The UGC Mukti Morcha began its protest from Mudi Chauraha in Agra district. The distance from there to the Agra collectorate is around 30 km. At Nadau Chauraha, about 3 km from the starting point, police blocked the road using JCB machines and hydras. The crowd broke through the barricade and moved ahead via different routes, reaching the Yamuna Expressway around 300 metres away. The protesters then blocked the expressway. There has been continued anger among members of the upper-caste community in villages linked to Etmadpur tehsil over the law. The protest is being led by UGC Mukti Morcha president Dharmendra Singh Chauhan, Raghavendra Singh, district panchayat member Manvendra Singh, Manoj Sikarwar, farmer leader Rajesh Sharma and Bharat Singh.

stories.title: Man kills brother for joking with his wife:He fed the BSc student, put him to bed in Gorakhpur, then hacked him to death
stories.summary: First-year BSc student in Gorakhpur was allegedly killed by his cousin over suspicions of an affair with the accused’s wife. The accused, Santosh Mishra, allegedly killed his cousin Kartikeya Mishra alias Shubham (19) while he was sleeping inside the house on September 17. Police arrested Santosh on Saturday on suspicion. During questioning, he allegedly confessed to the crime. He told police that Shubham used to joke and chat extensively with his wife, who was Shubham’s sister-in-law. He said he once read their chats on his wife’s phone and then suspected that the two were having an affair. Santosh said he tried to counsel them, but they did not listen. He said he had never had an argument with his wife during their 14-year marriage, but tensions had developed between them over the past three months. According to Santosh, he first fed Shubham a meal. After Shubham fell into a deep sleep, he allegedly attacked him four times with a sickle, killing him. The incident took place in the Bansgaon police station area, around 40km from the district headquarters. Accused said, 'I counselled my wife after reading their chats' Santosh is a resident of Jayantipur village. During questioning, he told police that Shubham was his cousin and that their houses were opposite each other. Santosh drives a vehicle for the village head. Shubham’s father, Swadesh Mishra, is a farmer and has been suffering from kidney disease for the past four to five years. Shubham’s family had gone to Lucknow for his kidney transplant and treatment. Shubham was alone at home, so I used to take food to him every day. However, since July, he had started joking and chatting excessively with my wife. Their body language was also different while talking and joking with each other. Seeing the change in their behaviour, I began to suspect both of them. One day, I read their chats on my wife’s phone. That was when I learnt about their alleged affair. I tried to counsel my wife about it, but we had an argument. She then attempted to die by suicide. I also counselled Shubham. When neither of them listened, I planned to kill Shubham. Went to kill Shubham on September 15, but failed; attacked him two days later Santosh said, “I went to kill Shubham on the night of September 15, but he woke up. So, I returned home and waited for the right opportunity. On September 16, I again went to Shubham’s house at around 8pm to give him food and then returned. At around 5am on September 17, I went to his house again. Shubham was sleeping on a wooden cot inside the house. I repeatedly struck him on the head with a sickle and killed him. I then fled. Shortly afterwards, two of Shubham’s friends arrived to wake him up for their daily walk. They were shocked to see blood on the cot and raised an alarm, calling villagers to the spot. Police then sent the body for a post-mortem.” SP South Dinesh Puri said Shubham’s uncle, Nagendra Mishra, lodged an FIR after the incident. Eight teams were formed to crack the case. Police examined footage from more than 50 CCTV cameras and analysed the call detail records (CDRs) of around 300 mobile numbers. The investigation revealed a dispute between Santosh, his wife and Shubham. Police also found that the three had suddenly stopped communicating with each other, which further increased suspicion on Santosh. The team questioned around 27 villagers, who told police about the dispute between the three. After piecing together the CDRs and other clues, police detained Santosh. During questioning, he confessed to the crime. ₹20 lakh extortion demanded from father in 2021 Police said Shubham’s father, Swadesh Mishra, ran a sweet shop in the town. In 2021, he was allegedly asked to pay ₹20 lakh in extortion. Gangster Shani Singh was accused in the case. After an FIR was registered, police provided security to the family. Following Shubham’s murder, police also investigated this angle.

stories.title: ‘Anyone harassing girls signs his own death warrant’:Yogi warns; says one took exam, another got recruited
stories.summary: CM Yogi said in Lucknow, “Today, no one can dare to harass a daughter. If someone does, he knows the consequences. If he does not know, I think he is signing his own death sentence.” He said, Before 2017, there was a lack of transparency in recruitment. There was nepotism. One person would take the recruitment exam, but someone else would get the appointment. So whenever recruitment was announced, young people would wonder how they could get a job without recommendations or a transaction. But that is no longer the case. The CM said, “You can keep counting; we have provided 9.5 lakh jobs. In the next six months, one lakh young people will receive joining letters. There are no riots in the state now. We sometimes conduct mock riot drills so that people do not forget how riots happen.” On Sunday, Yogi handed over appointment letters at Lok Bhavan to 912 candidates selected for the posts of Police Sub-Inspector (Confidential), Assistant Sub-Inspector (Clerk) and Assistant Sub-Inspector (Accounts). Yogi’s 5 major points 1- No mafia can now openly roam around brandishing weapons Yogi said that if the police recruitment process is transparent, changes can be brought about in the system. Before 2017, people from Uttar Pradesh were even hesitant to identify themselves as being from the state outside UP. The state witnessed riots and prolonged curfews. Riots continued for long periods in several places, including Bareilly, Aligarh and Muzaffarnagar. The influence of the mafia had become such a challenge that even administrative, police and judicial officials faced difficulties. The vehicles of judicial officials were even stopped in front of mafia convoys. “Can any mafia member today openly roam around brandishing a weapon or dare to start a riot? Earlier, those who could afford it would send their daughters outside to study. Those who could not afford it were forced to keep their daughters at home because they feared that a miscreant might harass them if they went outside.” 2- Recruitment was earlier affected by nepotism Yogi said the change in Uttar Pradesh’s perception had been brought about by the UP Police, which has become a symbol of trust for 250 million people. “People say they want to replicate the UP model. This change has come through reforms in the police force.” He said that in 2017, more than half of the police posts were vacant and recruitment had been stayed by the High Court and Supreme Court. Against the requirement of 400,000 police personnel, the state had only around 200,000. Recruitment had earlier been affected by nepotism. 3- Police personnel used to sleep under tiled roofs The CM said police barracks were also in poor condition earlier. When he personally visited to inspect them in Lucknow, he found police personnel sleeping under tiled roofs. “That is when we realised that changes were needed in the police system.” Subsequently, barracks were arranged in the police lines of every district. Large police barracks have been built in 56 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Police lines that had remained pending for decades were also constructed. “The police line is the backbone of the police force.” He said the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) had earlier been disbanded and its 34 companies were scrapped. “We reconstituted them. Today, whenever elections are held anywhere, 20 to 40 companies of police are sought from Uttar Pradesh.” 4- Those who could not accomplish anything will keep talking Yogi said irregularities in the recruitment process before 2017 had left young people disappointed and frustrated. Questions were first raised over the transparency of recruitment and later over the selection process. Cases of paper leaks had also come to light. In 2017, the government decided to make the recruitment process transparent and introduce reforms. Changes were made to the procedures of recruitment commissions and boards. The interview system for Group 3 and Group 4 posts was abolished. “Those who could not accomplish anything will keep talking. Those who made Uttar Pradesh a BIMARU state because of their incompetence have no right to speak about the UP Police. Uttar Pradesh and the country have already seen their incompetence.” 5- 110 acres of police land had also been encroached upon One of the biggest challenges for the UP Police is cyber security. Cyber police stations have been established in every district to tackle this. “The UP Police has achieved what once seemed impossible. Every day, we face new challenges.” A forensic institute was established in Uttar Pradesh. Earlier, the state had only two forensic laboratories. While searching for land for the forensic institute, it was discovered that police land had been encroached upon. An investigation found that 110 acres of police land had been registered in someone else’s name in revenue records and preparations were underway for plotting. The government lodged an FIR. After this, the person concerned surrendered and agreed to return the land. Uttar Pradesh now has police commissionerates in seven cities. “Before 2017, this could not even have been imagined. Earlier, a file would keep moving from one desk to another for years, with someone or the other putting a remark on it. One file had been pending since 1973. After this, the police commissionerate system was implemented in seven cities.” Finance Minister Khanna recited a shayari, ‘Yogi ji ke zehan mein taqat hai…’ Finance Minister Suresh Khanna recited a shayari: “Yogi ji ke zehan mein taqat hai, jab imaan ki, kyon na phir UP bane pehchaan Hindustan ki.” He said recruitment conducted before 2017 often remained surrounded by controversy and doubts. Allegations of irregularities and recommendations had surfaced. He said new employees should be satisfied that they had received this opportunity on the basis of merit. “In a government job, duty comes before rights. If someone comes to you with a grievance, treat them with sensitivity.” He said there was no place for arrogance in the police service. “Pride in one’s position brings a person down. Therefore, work with responsibility. If you work on time and responsibly, you will earn respect. Negligence, on the other hand, will lead to criticism and humiliation.” DGP said, ‘Appointment letter is not just a job, but a responsibility’ DGP Rajeev Krishna said that ministerial staff play an important role, just like police field units. “The appointment letter is not merely a letter of entry into a job; it also carries the responsibility of strengthening the Uttar Pradesh Police system.” He said that before 2017, the police had the capacity to train 6,000 constables, which has now increased to 60,244. From 2017 to now, 256,258 direct recruitments and 154,572 promotions have been made in the non-gazetted category. The process for 35,000 direct recruitments and more than 9,000 promotions is currently underway. He said police establishments, police lines, barracks and mess facilities have also been expanded since 2017. A large number of hostels have been built along with residential buildings at 74 police stations. “The objective is to create an environment where police personnel can work with ease.”

stories.title: Sub-inspector’s lawyer wife found hanging:Had love marriage 10 months ago in Prayagraj; he says she hanged herself
stories.summary: Sub-inspector’s wife was found hanging inside their flat in Prayagraj. She was a lawyer at the Allahabad High Court. According to the officer, the couple had an argument on Saturday. At around 8pm, his wife went into the room and locked the door from inside. Shortly afterwards, a family friend called and told him that Kanchan had messaged saying she was going to die by suicide. The sub-inspector said, “I called out to her and knocked on the door. When there was no response, I broke open the door. I found my wife’s body hanging inside.” Police reached the spot and sealed the flat. The incident took place at Paras Green Apartment in Dhoomanganj. Kanchan Singh, 33, was a lawyer at the High Court. She had a love marriage with sub-inspector Jitendra Singh 10 months ago. Jitendra is posted at Dhoomanganj police station. Parents tried to counsel her and left for Kanpur, then she locked herself in the room Sub-inspector Jitendra Singh, a resident of Kanpur, said, “My wife was also from Kanpur. I joined the police as a sub-inspector in the 2023 batch. We lived in a flat on the ninth floor of Paras Green Apartment. We had been having disagreements over something for the past few days. “After this, Kanchan’s parents came to Prayagraj from Kanpur. They stayed with us for three days and tried to counsel her. They left for Kanpur at around 8pm on Saturday. After they left, Kanchan went into the room and locked the door from inside. “Shortly afterwards, a family friend called me. Kanchan was representing the friend in a divorce case. He told me that Kanchan was going to hang herself. I immediately broke open the door, took my wife down and informed the police.” Messaged a friend, ‘I am going to die by suicide’ According to police, the sub-inspector and Kanchan first met while she was appearing for an examination at a college. The college where she went to take her LLB exam is run by the sub-inspector’s family. They started talking there and exchanged phone numbers. They later began speaking over the phone. Their friendship turned into a relationship within a few days, and they got married in a love marriage around 10 months ago. Five days ago, Kanchan and the sub-inspector had an argument over an issue. When the situation worsened, sub-inspector Jitendra called Kanchan’s family from Kanpur. Her family left on Saturday night. Jitendra said, “At around 11.45pm, a family friend called me and said that my wife Kanchan had sent him a message saying she was going to die by suicide. I immediately ran to her room, but the door was locked from inside. When I broke open the door, I found her body hanging.” He said several missed calls from one of his wife’s friends were also showing on her mobile phone. DCP City Sagar Jain said, Police reached the spot as soon as they received the information and carried out an investigation. Fingerprints and other evidence have been collected from the scene. The family members have also reached the spot. The apartment has been sealed for now. The body is being sent for post-mortem. Further action will be taken after the report is received.

stories.title: Youth dies while running during Home Guard recruitment exam:Wife says, 'He had BTech, BEd and TET qualifications but wanted a government job'
stories.summary: “My husband had passed BTech, BEd, CTET and UP-TET. He earned good money by running a coaching centre, but he wanted to get a government job. After celebrating his birthday on 17 September, he went to Moradabad to take part in the Home Guard recruitment race. The next day, we learnt that he had died. If I had even the slightest suspicion that he would not return, I would never have let him go.” As she said this, Komal Yadav of Bareilly began to cry. Her husband, Shivam Yadav, 27, collapsed on the ground while running during the physical test for Home Guard recruitment on 18 September. He was taken to hospital, where he died. Shivam’s father, Vinod, said- There were no adequate medical arrangements at the recruitment venue. When my son’s condition deteriorated, he was not even allowed inside. My son could not receive timely treatment. That is why he died. Dainik Bhaskar visited Shivam’s neighbourhood, Subhash Nagar, on Saturday. His home was steeped in mourning. His mother, Mamta Yadav, was distraught and lying in the courtyard. His father and wife were also grieving. We spoke to the family and learned about their loss. See two pictures- Got married five years ago and has a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter Shivam married five years ago. He has a two-and-a-half-year-old daughter, Shaili. He was the second of four brothers. His elder brother Ankit and younger brother Sachin are lawyers, while the youngest, Aditya, is still in Class 4. Told his wife we will celebrate your birthday in grand style next time His wife, Komal, said, “Shivam taught Physics, Chemistry and Maths to high school and intermediate students. He had also appeared for the preliminary and main examinations for railway loco pilot and was preparing for the next stage. He had also appeared for the lekhpal and Railway Group D examinations, but their results had not been announced.” He observed a fast on his birthday on 17 September. After breaking his fast, he told her, “We will celebrate your birthday in grand style next time.” He got dressed at 10.30 pm and caught a bus at 11 pm to pursue his government job. The next day, his body arrived. ‘By the time I reached the spot, my son had collapsed on the ground’ Shivam’s father, Vinod Yadav, said, “My son had a Home Guards physical test at the 9th PAC ground on Kanth Road in Moradabad. He had to complete a 4.8-kilometre run. I was informed that my son’s condition had deteriorated during the 12th round. I then reached the gate of the recruitment venue, but police personnel stopped me.” He said, “I pleaded to be allowed inside, but I was refused. I kept crying and begging at the gate, asking them to let me in, but the policemen kept driving me away. I was still not allowed inside for a long time. By the time I reached him, my son had fallen to the ground. There were not enough treatment facilities at the recruitment centre.” The father said, “I could see only one or two doctors. The ambulance drivers were wearing khaki uniforms. My son lay there for a long time. He was later taken to hospital. Even there, I was not allowed to meet him for a long time.
