stories.title: UP ATS kills Naxal carrying ₹30 lakh bounty:NIA had been hunting him for 8 years; opened fire when commandos cornered him in Kashi
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) killed suspected Naxal commander Brijesh Ganjhu alias Gopal Singh in an encounter in Varanasi. A ₹30 lakh bounty had been announced for information leading to his arrest. He was a commander of the banned Tritiya Prastuti Committee (TPC), a Naxalite outfit active in Jharkhand. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) had declared him wanted in a terror-funding case eight years ago. The encounter took place at around 4am on Sunday in the Ramnagar police station area. ATS DSP Vipin Rai said the team received information that the Naxal was travelling towards Mughalsarai via Ramnagar. ATS commandos then set up a cordon. During this, he arrived on a motorcycle with an associate. Rai said the team signalled them to stop, following which Brijesh allegedly opened fire with a pistol using both hands, fearing arrest. A bullet hit the bulletproof jackets of the DSP and Head Constable Nitendra Krishna. The team then retaliated, hitting Brijesh, who fell on the road. His associate fled the spot. Brijesh was taken to a district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Brijesh Ganjhu, 46, was a resident of the Lawalong police station area in Jharkhand’s Chatra district. He was allegedly involved in extorting money from transporters, coal mining companies and contractors. The Jharkhand government had announced a ₹25 lakh bounty on him, while the NIA had announced ₹5 lakh. His house was attached eight years ago. See pictures on encounter- Two pistols and several live cartridges recovered from Naxal ATS recovered two pistols from Naxal commander Brijesh Ganjhu. Several live cartridges and empty shell casings were also found in his possession. The ATS has kept his body at the Lal Bahadur Shastri post-mortem house. ADG Law and Order Amitabh Yash said that following the operation, the ATS and local police have stepped up security in the area. Know about Naxal commander Brijesh Ganjhu

stories.title: UP BJP sidelines CD controversy-hit Upendra Rawat:Santosh-Tawde formula seen in 98 district in-charges; old faces return
stories.summary: The BJP in Uttar Pradesh is now fully in election mode. On Saturday, the party appointed in-charges for all 98 organisational districts. The list issued by state president Pankaj Chaudhary includes several MLCs and former office-bearers. During their recent visits to Lucknow, the party's national general secretary (organisation), BL Santosh, and general secretary Vinod Tawde had urged the party to reactivate its old workers and former office-bearers. They said experienced former workers needed to be brought back into active roles for the election, otherwise they would remain at home, which could harm the party. The impact of Santosh and Tawde's message is visible in the list of district in-charges. State president Pankaj Chaudhary has appointed several former state office-bearers who were left out of his team as district in-charges. Former state general secretaries Govind Narayan Shukla and Subhash Yaduvansh are clear examples. Govind has been made in-charge of the state headquarters, while Subhash has been appointed social media in-charge. Former state vice-presidents Vijay Bahadur Pathak and Manvendra Singh assigned district responsibilities Nine MLCs appointed district in-charges The BJP has appointed Legislative Council members, or MLCs, Ashok Kataria, Anup Gupta, Manvendra Pratap Singh, Rajnikant Maheshwari, Santosh Singh, Pranshu Dutt Dwivedi, Vijay Bahadur Pathak, Arun Pathak and Dharmendra Singh as district in-charges. Upendra Rawat, who made headlines in the CD scandal, not given charge of a district Just before the 2024 Lok Sabha election, a video surfaced showing former Barabanki MP Upendra Rawat in an objectionable position with a foreign woman. The BJP subsequently cancelled his ticket. However, when the BJP released its list of state office-bearers in June, Rawat was appointed state general secretary. Those familiar with the matter believe the central leadership appointed Upendra Rawat as state general secretary despite opposition from state president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisational general secretary BL Santosh. However, Chaudhary and Dharampal have since not given Rawat any significant organisational responsibility. Most state general secretaries have been given charge of a region, but Rawat has not been assigned any region. He has also not been given charge of any front. Moreover, in the list of district in-charges released on Saturday, he was not assigned charge of any district either. Pooja Pal also not given charge of a district State vice-presidents Pooja Pal, Kritika Agrawal, Alok Gupta, Krishna Bihari Rai, Suresh Maurya and Rajesh Yadav have also not been made in charge of any district. State ministers Yatendra Sharma, Vijay Shivhare, Rajni Pandey, Rahul Valmiki, Ankur Sharma, Vijay Rajbhar, Kiran Bind Nishad, Rakesh Lodhi, Sanchita Chauhan, Aakanksha Sonkar, Subhashni Jaiswal and Deepmala Santoshi have also not been given charge of any district. To spend four months travelling across the districts According to BJP sources, a joint meeting of the party's district presidents and district in-charges will be held in the coming days. Responsibilities for the upcoming Assembly elections will be assigned at the meeting. With little time left before the Assembly elections, district in-charges will now have to spend four consecutive months touring their respective districts. They will also have to stay overnight in their districts at least three to four times a month to gather information about the political situation across all Assembly constituencies. Here is the list of organisational districts and in-charges by region Neeraj Singh tasked with reducing tensions in Raebareli Raebareli MP Rahul Gandhi is currently organising the 'Students' Voice' programme to connect young people across the country. The party has appointed its young face, Neeraj Singh, as in-charge of his constituency. Neeraj Singh has a large team of young people in Lucknow, Rae Bareli and several other districts of Awadh. There is intense rivalry between Cabinet Minister Manoj Pandey, Minister of State (Independent Charge) Dinesh Pratap Singh and MLA Aditi Singh in Rae Bareli. Neeraj Singh has been sent there to prevent clashes during the Assembly elections. Responsibility kept within organisational sphere While appointing district in-charges, the party has assigned most leaders responsibility for districts within their own organisational areas. This will allow them to travel to the districts more easily and give them a better understanding of the ground situation. Arun Pathak has been appointed in charge of Varanasi district and the Varanasi metropolitan area, Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency. Mahesh Shukla has been given responsibility for Gorakhpur metropolitan area, in Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's home district, while Ajay Singh Gautam has been given responsibility for Gorakhpur district. Rakesh Trivedi has been appointed in-charge of Prayagraj metropolitan area. District in-charges to report directly to Pankaj Chaudhary and Dharmapal All newly appointed district in-charges will travel to their respective districts and report directly to state president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisational general secretary Dharmapal Singh on organisational activities, campaigns and election-related issues. As a result, their political standing in the district will be higher than that of the district president. Pankaj Chaudhary and Dharampal had equal say In the list of district in-charges, state president Pankaj Chaudhary and organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh each had an equal say. Workers considered close to both leaders have been given responsibility as district in-charges. Earlier, the top leadership had also given importance to organisational general secretary Dharampal Singh's preferences in the list of state office-bearers. Several workers considered close to him were appointed as state office-bearers. Dharampal Singh also played a key role in forming the regional teams.

stories.title: Act if there are any violations: KTR
Crorepati farmer lives in luxury farmhouse:Class 10 dropout farms 250 acres; earns ₹1.65 crore from bananas alone
stories.summary: After failing Class 10, he dropped out of school. From traditional farming, he could save only ₹15,000-20,000 a year. Today, the same farmer is generating a turnover of crores. We are talking about Barabanki’s ‘Banana King’ and Padma Shri awardee Ramsharan Verma. Ramsharan, who promoted tissue-culture banana farming in Uttar Pradesh, has grown bananas on 55 acres this year. He claims to earn a profit of ₹3-4 lakh per acre. His farming techniques have become so popular that farmers from other states and even abroad visit his luxury farmhouse to learn his methods. When the Dainik Bhaskar team visited his farm, Ramsharan explained how an experiment in farming turned him into a ‘crorepati farmer’. Read the report… Farmers said – We adopted Ramsharan’s farming methods Daulatpur village is located 22 km from the Barabanki district headquarters. This is where farmer Ramsharan Verma has his farmhouse. The village has more banana, tomato and bottle gourd crops than wheat and paddy. At several places along the way, labourers could be seen loading bananas onto trucks near the fields. Farmers said around 2,500 people in the village are involved in farming. Until about 20 years ago, most people practised traditional farming, mainly growing wheat and paddy. Gradually, farmers began adopting Ramsharan’s methods. Today, most farmers in the village grow bananas, tomatoes and watermelons. The improved crop yields have increased farmers’ incomes and also changed their lifestyles. Started with 6 acres, now farming on 250 acres Ramsharan owns around 10 acres of land. We asked him how much land he farms and how much profit he makes. He said, “Initially, we had six acres of land. Later, we bought another 3-4 acres. After that, we started farming on land taken from farmers in the village on a cooperative basis.” “At present, we are farming on 250 acres. This year, bananas were planted on 55-57 acres. In terms of profit, we earned ₹3-4 lakh per acre this year.” If the minimum profit of ₹3 lakh per acre is calculated for 55 acres, the amount comes to ₹1.65 crore. Ramsharan further said, “Every year, we spend ₹3-4 crore. Sometimes the returns are ₹5-6 crore and sometimes they go up to ₹7 crore. So you can say that we are crorepati farmers. We built this luxurious farmhouse from farming income.” When we asked him about his farming methods, he smiled and said, “Farming techniques are best discussed in the field.” Failed Class 10 and quit studies; started farming in 1988 We accompanied Ramsharan to his banana field and asked him whether he had always been a farmer and if he had studied. He said, “I failed Class 10 and quit my studies. I have been farming since 1988. At that time, our family had six acres of land. We mainly grew wheat and paddy. Even after working hard, we could save only ₹15,000-20,000.” “Then I came to know about farmers in Gujarat and Maharashtra. I travelled there, stayed with farmers and learnt about their farming methods. After returning, I started farming using tissue-culture technology in Uttar Pradesh. It has been around 32 years since I started using this technique.” Tissue culture helps bananas mature faster When asked about tissue culture, Ramsharan said, “Other banana crops take around 15 months to mature, but this crop is ready in 11-12 months. Since Uttar Pradesh experiences winter, you can consider it 12-13 months here. In Gujarat, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, the crop is ready in 11-12 months.” Explaining its benefits, he said, “Time is important in everything. We plant this crop between June 15 and July 15. It is ready by August-September the following year. This period coincides with festivals, when banana consumption increases, so prices are also better.” “Because of the heat, our bananas reach a size of 22-23 cm, so we easily get ₹15-16 per kg.” ‘50,000 farmers are using our techniques’ Ramsharan said, “Every year, 14,000-15,000 farmers come to me. They see the crops, ask many questions, and then try the same methods in their own fields.” “At present, 50,000 farmers are using our techniques to farm across 2.5 lakh hectares. A farmer from Ambedkar Nagar visited us recently. He said he had planted bananas after learning from us and sold bananas worth ₹24 lakh from three acres.” “We have also created employment opportunities in the village for people who do not go to cities for work. That is a good thing.” Ramsharan advises farmers not to grow a single crop if they have 3-4 acres of land. “Never plant only one crop. In India, weather plays a 50% role in farming. Sometimes storms, hailstorms, or rain can destroy an entire crop. If you grow potatoes or tomatoes along with bananas, the weather may damage one crop while another survives. Last year, a storm in Maharashtra caused heavy damage to banana crops.” Has received Padma Shri and several other awards Ramsharan Verma has received several awards for his contribution to agriculture. He was awarded the Padma Shri in 2019. Before that, he received the Jagjivan Ram Kisan Puraskar from the Government of India, along with the Agriculture Leadership Award. He has also received the Chaudhary Charan Singh Kisan Samman, Udyan Pandit Award and Nav-Anveshak Samman Award from the Uttar Pradesh government. Apart from these, Ramsharan has received awards recognising him as an ideal farmer in Uttarakhand and Haryana. He has displayed all these awards at his farmhouse. Ramsharan describes himself as a non-political person. He said, “Even when politicians meet us, they talk only about farming and agriculture. That is what we like.”

stories.title: Surendra Koli found hanging after escaping death sentence:Lived as Sadaram where he opened shop; spent 19 years in jail
stories.summary: In November 2025, the Supreme Court, while hearing the famous Noida Nithari case, said that no matter how strong the suspicion is, it cannot replace solid evidence. Following this observation, Surendra Koli, who had been sentenced to death in 13 cases, was acquitted. After spending 19 years in jail, Koli returned to his village in Uttarakhand after his release. He changed his identity and opened a tea stall in Haridwar. On September 18, news suddenly emerged that Surendra Koli, an accused in the Nithari case, had died by suicide by hanging. Now the questions are: Why did he take such a step? On what grounds did the court acquit him? What did he do after being released from jail? By the time he was released, his family had fallen apart After the Supreme Court acquitted him, Surendra Koli walked out of Luksar Jail in Greater Noida on November 12, 2025. From there, he went to his brothers in Delhi. He then returned to his home in Mangrukhhal village in Almora, Uttarakhand. His life had changed completely since 2006. His mother had died. His wife, Shanti Devi, had remarried in 2015. They had a daughter, who had also got married. When Koli went to jail, Shanti was pregnant and later gave birth to a son. Surendra first saw his son inside the jail. Koli's ancestral house had turned into a ruin, so he stayed at the home of his younger brother, Anand Koli. After working as a labourer in Almora for a few days, he moved to Roshanabad in Haridwar. There, he ran a food cart for some time. However, the business did not do well. In June, Surendra organised a religious ceremony in his village. His other three brothers attended the ceremony with their families. Surendra's 19-year-old son was also there with his father. The man who helped him did not know he was Surendra Koli Surendra could not find a permanent place to stay in Haridwar. His food business also failed. In Roshanabad, he met Jai Kashyap. Surendra introduced himself as Sadaram and asked Jai to help him find work and a room to stay in. Jai helped him find a room, after which Surendra started working as a security guard at a factory. When the owner of the room asked him for his Aadhaar card, Surendra refused and had to leave. Through another acquaintance, Dharmendra Kaushik, he found a security guard's job at an apartment in Haridwar. However, he could not continue successfully at these places either. He was also diabetic and remained troubled by his health. Just five days earlier, on September 15, he had rented a small shop near Saptarishi police outpost in Haridwar. The monthly rent was ₹7,000. After paying two months' rent in advance, he opened the shop. But just four days later, he died by suicide by hanging himself inside the same shop. It was initially said that the shop fell in an encroachment area and had to be removed because of preparations for the Haridwar Kumbh. However, it has now emerged that this was not the case. The shop he had rented had previously been an Aanchal Milk outlet and was built according to the required standards, so there was no possibility of it being removed. Narayan Singh Rawat, a former district panchayat member who helped Koli legally, says Surendra was troubled by the shop owner and had accused him of harassment. He had called and said the shopkeeper was troubling him and asking to increase the rent. Narayan Singh said Surendra was financially weak, so they had recently helped him with ₹25,000. Why did the court acquit Surendra Koli? In 2014, Surendra Koli was sentenced to death in the first case by the district court, Allahabad High Court and later the Supreme Court. At the time, a mercy petition was sent to President Pranab Mukherjee, who also rejected it. On September 2, 2014, a death warrant was issued in Koli's name. On September 4, he was shifted to the barrack at Meerut's Dasna Jail where he was scheduled to be hanged on September 12. However, at the last moment, it was decided that the execution would take place on the morning of September 8. An executioner was also appointed. On the night of September 7, lawyer Indira Jaisingh approached the Supreme Court. The court opened at 1 am, and then Chief Justice HL Dattu heard the matter. Indira Jaisingh argued that if Koli was executed in the first case, how would justice be done in the remaining 12 cases? The court stayed the execution for a week. When court commuted death sentence to life imprisonment The case took a new turn in 2015 when the Allahabad High Court commuted his death sentence to life imprisonment, citing an excessive delay in deciding his mercy petition. However, he was subsequently sentenced to death in 11 other cases. After he was sentenced in all the cases, the Allahabad High Court made an observation in 2023. The court said several pieces of evidence in the case were not sufficiently reliable. Since the two accused had already spent 17 years in prison, they were acquitted. The victims' families objected to the decision, and the CBI challenged it in the Supreme Court. While delivering its verdict, the court said what happened in Nithari was serious, but under criminal law, guilt cannot be established solely on the basis of suspicion or conjecture. Conviction requires admissible and reliable evidence. The court said that no matter how strong the suspicion is, it cannot replace solid evidence. Did negligence and delay weaken the entire investigation? Advocate Paras Nath Singh, who represented Surendra Koli, said the case lacked circumstantial evidence. He said the confessions recorded by the CBI were not considered reliable by the court. Under the law, a confession must be made voluntarily and not under fear or pressure. Page 47 of the 308-page order says Koli remained in police custody for 60 days, but he was never medically examined during this period. This left doubts about the possibility of physical torture. A medical certificate from 2007 was produced, but the doctor concerned was not presented to establish its reliability. The court said that initially, Moninder Singh Pandher and Surendra Koli were held responsible for the things found at the crime scene. However, over time, Koli alone came to be blamed for everything. The witnesses who appeared before the court also kept changing their statements. Eventually, Koli's confession became the main basis of the case, even though its reliability was already under question. On November 11, 2025, Chief Justice BR Gavai, while ruling on the last pending case against Koli, said that the same evidence which the court had found insufficient and unreliable while acquitting him in the first 12 cases could not constitutionally be used to keep him convicted in the remaining case. Chief Justice Gavai also questioned the investigation process followed by the police and agencies. He said that if an investigation is conducted on time, professionally and in accordance with constitutional principles, the truth can be uncovered even in the most difficult cases. But that did not happen in the Nithari case. Negligence and delay weakened the entire investigation and closed the routes that could have led investigators to the actual perpetrators.

stories.title: 35 IPS officers, 31 PPS transferred in UP:Pregnant Charu Nigam transferred to PAC Ghaziabad
stories.summary: The Yogi government has transferred 35 IPS and 31 PPS officers. Several cities have received new city SPs. Charu Nigam, SP of UP 112, has been appointed commandant of the 47th Battalion PAC in Ghaziabad. IPS officer Charu had previously served as the commandant of this unit. Charu Nigam is currently pregnant. Before joining UP 112, Charu Nigam was the SP of Sultanpur. When she was transferred from there, she expressed her pain in an X post. She wrote: As I bid farewell to Sultanpur, I want to make it clear that becoming a mother is not a weakness but a strength. Despite being pregnant, during my 197-day tenure in Sultanpur, I was capable of handling the responsibility of the district with full efficiency. Charu Nigam, a 2013-batch IPS officer, had been Sultanpur district's Superintendent of Police (SP) since February. On 20 August, the government transferred her to UP 112. During her six-month tenure in Sultanpur, the large-scale transfer and posting of police personnel and her dispute with BJP MLC Devendra Singh remained in the headlines. stories.title: Lover stabs woman supervisor to death:Had moved from Prayagraj to Jharkhand for job 5 months ago; father faints on hearing news
stories.summary: An Anganwadi supervisor from Prayagraj was stabbed to death in Jharkhand. She was working as a supervisor there and lived in a rented room. On Thursday (17 September) afternoon, her boyfriend arrived at her room and stabbed her to death. The landlord, who reached the spot after hearing screams, caught the boyfriend. The boyfriend is from Mirzapur and has been arrested by the police. The Anganwadi supervisor had joined her job in Jharkhand only five months ago. After the post-mortem, her body was brought to her ancestral village at around noon on Saturday, triggering cries of grief. At around 3 pm, Anita’s body was cremated at Dengurpur Ganga Ghat in Manda. Her father lit the funeral pyre but soon fainted and collapsed. The case is under the jurisdiction of Manda police station. When the Anganwadi supervisor’s body was brought to her ancestral village at noon on Saturday, the atmosphere was filled with grief as family members and villagers broke down in tears. Read the full case in detail Anita Bind, 27, daughter of Kashi Prasad Bind of Ulda village, had secured a job as an Anganwadi supervisor 5 months ago. She was posted at the Women and Child Development Project Office in Sonua block, Chakradharpur, Jharkhand. She lived in a rented house in Gwala Patti, Sheetla Temple, Ward-7, Chakradharpur, West Singhbhum. Anita was unmarried. She was the second eldest among four siblings. Her father, Kashi Bind, and her brother, Shyam Bind (35), work as tailors in Ulda village. Her younger brother, Adarsh (24), is studying. Her younger sister, Geeta (21), looks after the work of the gram panchayat. Lover went to her room and killed her At around 2 p.m. on 17 September, Anil Kumar Bind, a resident of the Jigna police station area in Mirzapur district, went to meet Anita at her room in Jharkhand. Meanwhile, hearing screams from the room, landlord Sanjay Saw and local residents reached the house on the upper floor. Anil then ran out of the room and tried to flee. Anita's body, brutally stabbed with a knife, was lying in the room. People caught Anil and handed him over to the police. They had been having an affair for three years During police questioning, Anil identified himself as Anita's lover. The two had been having an affair for three years. Police are linking the incident to the affair. According to Chakradharpur police station in-charge Avnish Bhagora of Jharkhand, a case has been registered, and an investigation has begun. The lover is being questioned. So far, the matter has emerged as a murder linked to the affair.

stories.title: Teacher fumes at students for chanting ‘Jai Shri Ram’:Says, ‘So many gods, who will save you in crisis?’; Bajrang Dal surrounds college
stories.summary: In Kasganj, a teacher has been accused of stopping students from saying "Jai Shri Ram" and reprimanding them. According to the students, a discussion on a subject related to God was taking place in the classroom at around 11 a.m. on Saturday. During the discussion, the students expressed their views by saying "Jai Shri Ram". It is alleged that the teacher reprimanded them and told them not to say "Jai Shri Ram". The teacher asked, given that Hinduism has so many gods and goddesses, who would come to save them in times of crisis? After college ended, the students informed Bajrang Dal workers about the incident. After this, a large number of workers reached the college and created a commotion. The workers also raised slogans of "Jai Shri Ram" on the college premises. They told the teacher, "Do you come here to teach or to do all this? If Ram and Lakshman do not come, will Allah come to save you?" After the matter reached the principal, the teacher has been asked to provide an explanation regarding the entire incident. Now read the full details The incident took place at Sant Tulsidas Municipal Inter College in Soronji. Janardan Ram teaches social science at the college and has been posted there for the past five years. Students have accused the teacher of hurting religious sentiments and presenting history incorrectly. Class 9 student Pranshu said, "When students raised the slogan 'Jai Shri Ram' in class, teacher Janardan Ram began scolding them. He said, 'If you want to pray, go home.' He also said that some people talk about one god coming, while others talk about another, but there should be only one God." Teacher says, "My words were misunderstood" Teacher Janardan Ram rejected the allegations. He said he was explaining a story and examples to the children in class and telling them about the beliefs of different religions. "While giving an example, I said that God is worshipped in Islam and Jesus Christ in Christianity. I had spoken to the children in this context, but my words were misunderstood." Teacher says-My words were misunderstood Janardan Ram said Hinduism recognises many gods and goddesses. To explain this, he asked the children who would come to save a person in distress from among so many gods and goddesses. He had asked the question only as an example. He had no intention of hurting anyone's religious sentiments. However, the children misunderstood what he said. Bajrang Dal demands impartial investigation Bajrang Dal district convenor Govind Mahere said, "Religious discrimination and comments on deities will not be tolerated in an educational institution. An impartial investigation should be conducted into the matter and action should be taken against the teacher." College principal Ram Karan said that the teacher had been issued a notice. He has to submit his response within three days. Further action will be taken after his response is received. No complaint has been filed with the police in the matter so far.

stories.title: Lucknow gang posed as FBI agents to dupe Americans:Victims were made to transfer funds in gold, dollars, and crypto; 16 accused from 5 states arrested
stories.summary: Police have busted a fake international call centre in Aliganj, Lucknow. The gang members claimed to be agents of the US investigative agency FBI, FDI officers, and representatives of major companies such as Microsoft and Amazon. They then lured foreign nationals, particularly Americans, into their trap by calling them. They intimidated the victims by telling them that they were involved in drug and pornography scandals. They got the fraud money transferred in the form of gold, cryptocurrency, and dollars. Aliganj police arrested 16 accused in the case on Friday. On Saturday, police held a press conference to disclose the details of the incident. Police have registered a case against 17 people, including gang leader Shiva alias Priyanshu Kushwaha, under the IT Act and 11 sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. According to police, the gang has committed fraud worth crores. The main accused, Shiva alias Priyanshu Kushwaha, is absconding. He is a resident of Gujarat. See the pictures after the call centre was busted... Targeted victims by posing as FBI and FDI officers The gang was operating the centre under the name NEXOLANE SOLUTION. The online data of foreign nationals was tracked from there. To carry out the fraud, fake pop-ups and hacking alerts were sent to their computers or mobile phones. Victims' calls reached the call centre through the number or option provided in the pop-up. The accused then spoke to them while posing as Microsoft agents or global technical support representatives. Claiming that they would fix a problem with the computer, they gained access to it using remote-access software such as UltraViewer. A fake security scan was then carried out. Victims were told that pornography websites had been accessed from their computers or that evidence of illegal activities such as child pornography and drug smuggling had been found. This frightened the victims. After the agents, the verification and closure teams took over The gang operated at three levels. First, the agents spoke to the victims. Their information was passed on to the verification team. The verifiers contacted the victims again to confirm the details. The case was then handed over to the closure team. Members of the closure team claimed to be officials of the FBI, the US Treasury Department, or other government departments. They extorted money from the victims by threatening them with arrest and legal action. They collected payments in dollars, gold, and cryptocurrency In the name of closing the case and providing protection, the gang asked victims to send gift cards by email, which were later converted into cryptocurrency and transferred by gang leader Shiva Kushwaha to his accounts through QR codes. Those who were unable to make online transactions were made to send dollars or gold by parcel or courier to the gang's agents in the US. Accused hail from Gujarat, Bengal, Bihar, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh According to the police, the call centre was being operated by the main accused, Shiva alias Priyanshu Kushwaha. He is a resident of Ahmedabad, Gujarat, and is currently absconding. Nehal and Ashish played key roles in the call centre's operations and management. They handled the hiring, training, and attendance arrangements for the employees. The arrested accused are residents of Gujarat, West Bengal, Bihar, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. Among them, manager Ashish and verifier/team in-charge Mayank Chauhan are residents of Ahmedabad. In addition, the police have registered an FIR against Vivek Singh, Aditya Kumar Singh, Shilpa Chakraborty, Rocky Rana, Ayushman, Hasnain, Vishal, Tasina Ghazi, Bishwajeet Mandal, Rehan alias Faran, Jennifer Lama, Joita Das, Suheb and Nehal Kumar. Employees working at the call centre were paid monthly salaries of ₹18,000 to ₹30,000. Their accommodation and meals were also provided free of charge. 36 laptops and 20 mobile phones recovered Items recovered included 36 laptops containing diallers, remote-access apps such as UltraViewer and Supremo, and fake FBI/FTC files; 20 mobile phones, which were collected in the manager's cabin as soon as employees entered the office; five Wi-Fi routers; 22 headphones; 20 mice; and 32 laptop chargers. Police have registered a case against all 17 accused under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for fraud, forgery, and criminal conspiracy) and under sections of the Information Technology (IT) Act. A search for the main accused, Shiva alias Priyanshu Kushwaha, and his other associates is underway, as is an investigation into their financial transactions. The police team that made the arrests was honoured with a cash reward of ₹25,000 by the Deputy Commissioner of Police (North). Constable Vipin Kumar Verma was separately given a cash reward of ₹5,000 for his better and commendable work.

stories.title: Internet fails during SSC exam in Agra:First shift starts after hours of waiting; angry students create ruckus
stories.summary: Internet services went down at the Khandari campus in Agra on Saturday during the Staff Selection Commission (SSC) Selection Post Phase 14 examination. As a result, the computer-based examination could not begin. Candidates waited for hours for the examination to start. Angry candidates created a commotion at the centre. Candidates for the first shift arrived at the examination centre in the morning. The examination could not begin because the systems could not be logged in. The staff said there was a problem with internet connectivity. The candidates remained seated in the lab for a long time. Their frustration grew as they received no clear response. The first-shift examination was eventually conducted after a considerable delay. Second-shift candidates also express anger The second-shift candidates also faced problems because of the disrupted internet service. A crowd gathered at the centre. The candidates kept asking whether the examination would be held. However, the university administration did not immediately provide any clear response. This further increased the anxiety among the second-shift candidates. Examinations to be held from 16 to 26 September It may be noted that the computer-based examination for SSC Selection Post Phase 14 is being held from 16 to 26 September. The examination is being conducted at various centres across the country. Khandari Campus in Agra is a major centre, and hundreds of candidates come here every day to take the examination.

stories.title: 13 PCS officers transferred in UP:Dinesh Kumar appointed ADM Ayodhya, Himanshu Gupta made BDA secretary
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government transferred 13 PCS officers on Saturday afternoon, with Dinesh Kumar, the chief revenue officer of Mau, appointed ADM City, Ayodhya, while the additional municipal commissioner of Mathura was given charge as ADM City, Kanpur. Himanshu Gupta, general manager of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation, has been appointed to head the Bareilly Development Authority. Pawan Kumar, general manager of the Uttar Pradesh Cooperative Sugar Mills Federation, has been appointed ADM Finance and Revenue, Kushinagar. Alok Kumar Gupta, ADM City of Kanpur Nagar, has been appointed ADM Finance and Revenue, Kasganj. Arun Kumar, additional district magistrate (judicial) of Chitrakoot, has been transferred to the post of joint director, administration, in the Fisheries Department. Kanchan Gupta, SDM of Mathura, has been given charge as sub-divisional magistrate (judicial) in Chitrakoot. Suraj Kumar Yadav, special officer on duty with the Board of Revenue, has been sent to Saharanpur. He has been appointed additional municipal commissioner. Jitendra Kataria, SDM of Pratapgarh, has been appointed deputy director, administration, Ayurveda. Vandita Srivastava, secretary of the Bareilly Development Authority, has been given the responsibility of deputy director at the Directorate of Higher Education in Prayagraj. Bhadohi SDM Bhan Singh has been transferred to Shahjahanpur, where he has been given the responsibility of additional commissioner in the Municipal Corporation.

stories.title: VIDEO | Car hits 5 students during stunt driving:Victims were standing by roadside in Noida, thrown onto bonnet; one suffers leg fracture
stories.summary: In Noida, a property dealer hit five students with a car while performing stunts. The impact was so forceful that the students were thrown into the air, landed on the car's bonnet and then fell onto the road. Seeing this, the accused increased the car's speed and fled. People ran after the car shouting, but he did not stop. One student suffered a broken leg, while four students sustained injuries to their heads, legs and hands. Police who reached the spot after receiving the information took all the injured students to hospital. The accident took place near the Knowledge Park police station on Friday evening. A video of the incident has emerged today. DCP Ravi Shankar Neem said: "The car driver has been identified from the video. A student was also sitting in the car with the accused property dealer, Manish. Both have been taken into custody and are being questioned." See three pictures Injured student's brother said, "They were performing stunts with three or four cars" Dujana resident Dhruv Nagar said, "My brother Gaurav Nagar is studying for a BCA at GNIOT College. Yesterday evening, he was passing near the college with his friends. At that time, some boys were performing stunts in three or four vehicles there." The people driving the vehicles could be seen suddenly braking on the road at times and turning the vehicles at others. Some people were filming this. When the people making the video had gone a little further, a speeding car came from behind. Before they could understand what was happening, the car hit them Dhruv Nagar said, "Before they could understand what was happening, the car hit five students, including my brother Gaurav, who was standing by the roadside." As soon as the collision occurred, screams rang out. The students had not even managed to get up when the driver turned the car around, accelerated and fled. "People ran after him shouting, "Catch him, catch him," but the accused did not stop the car. The police were then informed. The police reached the spot and took the injured to hospital in an ambulance. My brother's leg was fractured in the accident," Nagar said.

stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday (19 Sept) launched a sharp attack on Akhilesh Yadav and Shivpal Yadav in Lucknow. He said, “Earlier, the uncle-nephew duo would fearlessly set out to loot government jobs. Today, they are in the role of giving sermons. After 2027, they will not even remain in a position to preach.” Know what Yogi said… Yogi said: “Earlier, people could get jobs without even appearing for examinations. As soon as s were issued, contracts would be distributed and the business would begin. Those who created chaos in the distribution of appointment letters before 2017 should note that we are going to provide government jobs to more than one lakh young people in the next six months. stories.title: Tawde gives 3 mantras for 2027 victory:District chiefs must submit political, social and organisational analysis report
stories.summary: Formal preparations for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections have begun in the Gorakhpur region, with BJP national general secretary and Uttar Pradesh in-charge Vinod Tawde holding a series of meetings with party functionaries and elected representatives. The meetings are part of the party’s broader organisational exercise ahead of the polls. The main responsibility has been placed on organisational office-bearers. Tawde outlined three areas of analysis namely political, social and organisational and asked district presidents from 12 districts to focus on detailed ground-level assessment rather than relying only on data. The political analysis has been asked to be completed by October, with reports to be submitted thereafter. Political analysis to cover candidates, caste equations and BJP prospects The political analysis will cover every Assembly constituency in the districts. District presidents will assess potential strong contenders from each party, the candidates the Opposition may field, and which candidature could benefit the BJP. They will also study the caste equations in each area. The exercise will also identify influential local leaders whose entry could benefit the BJP during the election. Their names and the potential advantages of bringing them into the party will have to be included in the report. A similar assessment will be carried out at the booth level. District presidents have also been asked to compare the BJP’s position in their Assembly constituencies in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections and the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Where the BJP’s victory margin has narrowed compared with 2022, where the party has lost a seat, or where its margin of defeat has increased, the reasons will have to be analysed in detail. The broader Gorakhpur-region exercise is focused on assessing the party’s grassroots organisation, booth-level position and local political equations ahead of the 2027 polls. Tawde starts political outreach soon after reaching Gorakhpur Although Tawde’s formal meetings began on the second day of his visit, he started gathering political feedback soon after reaching Gorakhpur. He first met some senior leaders at his hotel to understand the local situation. He later visited the residence of Dr Radha Mohan Das Agrawal, a former BJP national general secretary and Rajya Sabha member who had represented Gorakhpur City as an MLA four times. The two held a detailed discussion over dinner on the political situation in Gorakhpur and neighbouring districts, including the strengths and weaknesses of the organisation. The meeting also gave Tawde an opportunity to draw on Agrawal’s two decades of experience as an MLA in Gorakhpur. ‘Do 100 tasks, but highlight only one’ At a meeting with regional and district office-bearers, Tawde stressed that merely creating an impression of work would not be enough. He said, “Office-bearers should not publicise one piece of work as if they had completed 100 tasks. If they have 100 responsibilities, they should focus on actually completing them rather than highlighting each one.” Tawde also asked every office-bearer to assess what contribution they would make to the election campaign. Responding to a question frequently raised by workers, he said that if a worker complained about not being heard at a police station, he should also consider whether he would be able to continue in the same position if an Akhilesh Yadav-led government returned to power. Tawde holds discussions with seven of 12 district presidents The BJP has 12 organisational districts in the Gorakhpur region, and Tawde held discussions with district presidents from seven of them. During the meeting, the district presidents stood up and briefed him on preparations in their respective districts. Most of them shared details such as the number of booths, the formation and verification of booth committees, and the status of Shakti Kendras. Tawde told them that providing data on organisational structures would not be enough and that the focus now had to shift towards detailed analysis. He outlined three areas of analysis, political, social and organisational. The BJP's Gorakhpur region comprises 12 organisational districts and covers 62 Assembly constituencies. As part of the social analysis, Tawde said office-bearers would have to understand the role and influence of social and religious organisations. Referring to factionalism in some districts, he said, “Avoid it. If you have any problem with someone, tell me privately.” ‘Analyse influential organisations and remain connected with people’ The exercise will include analysing which organisations have influence among people, which direction they are moving in, and what their internal meetings and public statements indicate. At the same time, party workers will have to maintain direct contact with people at the grassroots level. Explaining organisational analysis, Tawde said, “Every office-bearer from the booth level to the mandal and district levels must remain active. The party will also have to keep track of the activities of other political parties.” The district presidents with whom Tawde interacted included those from Deoria, Basti, Siddharthnagar, Kushinagar, Gorakhpur City and Gorakhpur district. ‘Turn difficult seats into triangular contests’ The meeting discussed a strategy for Assembly constituencies where the BJP may face a difficult direct contest. It was suggested that, at the local level, efforts should be made to create a three-cornered contest wherever possible. Similar electoral dynamics have previously affected contests in the region, where a divided opposition vote has influenced the outcome. The meeting also assessed that the Samajwadi Party’s position could be stronger than in the previous election and estimated that the party could begin the contest with more than 30% support. Focus on social media, young voters and local caste equations The meeting stressed that the BJP’s social media team should remain fully active. Any rumour or misleading information should be countered quickly with a factual response. The party was also advised to focus on young voters and study the local influence of Brahmin, Sainthwar and Nishad communities. The meeting also discussed reminding voters of past political experiences associated with Yadav-led governments.

stories.title: Suspended Jal Kal EE in Varanasi blames civic body:Minister suspended him over waterlogging; says pumps stopped due to flood
stories.summary: Varanasi Jal Kal's suspended executive engineer (EE) has questioned the action taken by Urban Development Minister AK Sharma. He said the waterlogging was caused by the Municipal Corporation's negligence, but he was made the scapegoat. The pump was shut down on 20 August after correspondence. This is done every year because of flooding. If everyone knew about this, how could it be my fault? Following his claim, Dainik Bhaskar visited the 140 MLD pump house in Chaukaghat to understand how it operates. It also tried to find out where the negligence occurred and whether the Jal Nigam or the Municipal Corporation was more responsible. Read the report... Pictures of the pump house Now read what suspended Executive Engineer (EE) Pawan Kumar Gupta said and what questions he raised... Pawan Kumar Gupta, who was posted at the 140 MLD pumping station in Chaukaghat, has now been attached to Kanpur. An inquiry is under way against the Jal Nigam EE. Speaking over the phone from Kanpur about his suspension, he raised a major question and said, Why is action being taken against a Jal Nigam engineer for the Municipal Corporation's negligence? The grounds for the suspension are not valid EE Pawan Kumar Gupta said, The grounds on which I was suspended are not valid. The reality is something else, but the issue has been diverted elsewhere. Sewers in the city are clogged, which is causing waterlogging. They do not have the resources to prevent waterlogging. Action was taken against us to conceal this fact, even though we operated the pumps. Chaukaghat pumping station built near the Varuna river Pawan Kumar Gupta said, The pumping station at Chaukaghat is near the Varuna river. This time, the Varuna's water level reached 71 metres. The entire area was waterlogged. Several times, Varuna's water has also entered the pump house. In such a situation, when we run the pumps, will we be able to pump out Varuna's water? Why has the water level of the Varuna risen? In such a situation, no matter how much we pump, it will not make any difference. So how will the sewage water be pumped out? They are accusing us to conceal their own shortcomings The suspended executive engineer said, All the sewers of the municipal corporation are choked and full. This is causing waterlogging in the city. To hide their own shortcomings, they have blamed us and said that the pump is not working. But when the Ganga's water level has risen, the pump cannot do anything. A large pumping station and a retaining wall should be built here. This is meant for sewage pumping, but they are making us pump floodwater. Find out what Ajay Kumar Sinha, the site in-charge of the Chowkaghat pumping station, said, Sewage from several parts of the city goes to the STP from here Ajay Kumar Sinha said, This is a 140 MLD sewage pumping station (urban). It mainly handles sewage collected from several places. Sewage lines from Phulwaria, the Cantonment, Lahurabir and several other parts of the city have been connected here. We pump it from here, separate the garbage and pump it to the STP. Primary treatment is carried out here before the sewage is sent for treatment. The garbage is then separated, after which it goes directly to the STP. Pumping stations are shut down during floods Ajay further said, This pumping station is related to river pollution. It was built to prevent the river from being polluted. The water from the city's drains and sewers used to flow into the rivers. It has to be intercepted and sent to the STP from here. This area lies along the Varuna, and when flooding occurs, the water level rises and the river merges with the drains. In such a situation, pumping is stopped so that no problem is caused in the river. We will not be able to treat that water because treating the river water and releasing it back into the river would serve no purpose. Letter issued on 20 August itself Ajay said that all pumping stations along the riverbanks are shut during floods. This station is operational. It is shut during floods, but when there is no flooding, it is not shut. This time, when the Ganga's water level rises above 68 metres, the line to this 140 MLD pump station is closed because of the reverse flow from the Varuna. Water from the Varuna then begins flowing into it. This year too, as in the past, our executive engineer received an order from the Dinapur STP stating that the river and drain had met on 20 August. It should therefore be shut and maintenance work carried out. It should be restarted once the water level falls. Heard of this for the first time in six years According to Ajay, this is the first time in six years that it has come to light that the closure of the SPS has caused waterlogging somewhere in the city. This is a new issue for us as well, so it is impossible to say anything at this stage. According to the documents and records available to us so far, whenever floodwater has arrived, not only this station but all pumping stations along the Ganga in the city have shut down.

stories.summary: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) papers were smuggled out of a printing press in Agra, Uttar Pradesh, hidden inside the soles of shoes. This has been revealed in Thane Police's 3,500-page charge sheet. The accused were paid ₹8,000 in return for taking the papers out. They were also promised land plots in Agra. Thane Police filed the charge sheet in the local court in Bhiwandi on Friday. Eighteen people, including mastermind Bijendra Gupta, have been named as accused. Gupta's name had earlier surfaced in a paper leak case in Odisha. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while Ashok Saw and Prakash Misal are absconding. The paper was leaked a day before the TET examination scheduled for 28 June. Following this, the Maharashtra State Examination Council (MSEC) postponed the examination. The papers were leaked from Agra's Mahim Patran Private Limited printing press DCP Pawan Bansod received information that three people were trying to sell the examination papers to a man from Bhiwandi. The police then arrested the accused in the Kongao area. They recovered four sets of the papers from them. Officials of the Maharashtra State Council of Examination (MSCE) confirmed during the investigation that the papers were genuine. According to the charge sheet, the papers were leaked from Agra's Mahim Patran Private Limited printing press. Confidential papers for the TET examination were being printed at this press. Between 15 and 17 June, two press employees and a former employee folded the pages of the papers and hid them in the soles of shoes. At the printing press, security guards searched the suspects' clothes but did not check their shoes. The suspects took advantage of this and smuggled the papers out. Four separate sets of the two TET papers had been prepared to prevent cheating in the examination. One of these sets was to be used on the day of the examination. The suspects had taken all four sets out of the printing press. What is the TET examination? The Teacher Eligibility Test, or TET, is a national-level eligibility examination that determines whether a candidate is qualified to become a teacher for primary and upper-primary classes, from Class 1 to Class 8. The National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE) made the examination mandatory in 2010. The Centre conducts Central TET, while states conduct State TET. The NCTE gave candidates appointed to teaching posts five years to qualify the TET, which was later reduced to four years. Candidates approached the court against the NCTE notice. In June 2025, a Madras High Court bench said that teachers appointed before 29 July 2011 would not be required to pass the TET to remain in service, but passing the TET would remain mandatory for promotion. The matter later reached the Supreme Court from different states. 2 September 2025: Supreme Court orders, ‘Teachers must pass the TET’ The Supreme Court said on 2 September last year that teachers must pass the TET (Teacher Eligibility Test) to remain in service or receive a promotion. A bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Manmohan said that all teachers with more than five years of service remaining would come under the rule. The court extended the deadline for passing the TET from 31 August 2027 to 31 August 2028. Those who fail to pass the TET will have to either resign or take compulsory retirement. The court issued these directions while exercising its special powers under Article 142.

stories.title: UP MLA Pooja Pal duped of ₹1.55 lakh:Money withdrawn via PhonePe; says personal data also at risk
stories.summary: Around ₹1.55 lakh was fraudulently withdrawn from the bank account of Pooja Pal, MLA from the Chail constituency in Kaushambi and BJP State Vice-President. The amount was deducted in multiple transactions between 22 August and 13 September via PhonePe and UPI. The MLA came to know about this on 14 September. Upon inspecting her bank account statement, several transactions were uncovered that had been executed without her knowledge. Following a complaint lodged by the MLA, an FIR was registered at the Dhoomanganj police station in Prayagraj on Friday at 2 pm. Money withdrawn multiple times over 22 days The MLA, Pooja Pal, holds an account with the Union Bank of India branch in Dhoomanganj, Prayagraj. She informed the police that money was fraudulently withdrawn from her account multiple times between 22 August and 13 September. The MLA suspects that someone hacked her iPhone 17 Air and misused her banking and personal data. The police, with the assistance of the cyber cell, are examining the mobile device, PhonePe, UPI, and bank account details. Demand for investigation into transactions and mobile device The MLA has requested the cyber crime police to conduct an investigation into all PhonePe and UPI transactions made between 22 August and 13 September. She has urged for a technical audit of her mobile phone, along with a review of all transaction IDs and bank account details. Furthermore, the MLA has demanded that future unauthorized withdrawals from her account be prevented and that the stolen sum of approximately ₹1.55 lakh be recovered. Copies of the complaint have also been submitted to the Cyber Crime Police Station in Prayagraj, the Dhoomanganj Police Station, and the manager of the concerned bank branch. The police are currently investigating the matter.

stories.title: SP MP’s car pelted with stones, windows smashed:Chaos during Ganesh Visarjan in Sant Kabir Nagar; people angry over DJ's detention
stories.summary: In Sant Kabir Nagar, a crowd vandalised the vehicle of SP MP Laxmikant alias Pappu Nishad during the visarjan of a Ganesha idol. The mob surrounded the vehicle and smashed its window. Police safely evacuated the MP from the crowd. The incident occurred on Friday night at around 11 pm. The visarjan procession had reached the Amardobha crossing. Meanwhile, the police began taking the DJ to the police station. Outraged by this, people sat on the road in protest. Just then, the MP's vehicle was passing through the area. The angry crowd surrounded his vehicle and vandalised it. Following the incident, a heavy police force was deployed in the area. Additional Superintendent of Police Sushil Kumar Singh and the Additional District Magistrate arrived at the spot and reasoned with the people. The incident took place within the jurisdiction of the Bakhira police station area. The MP stated, “All three of my vehicles were vandalised and stones were pelted. The miscreants are protected by the ruling party. They attacked after seeing the party flag and because I belong to a lower caste. Upper-caste people cannot tolerate how a man from a lower caste became an MP. A life-threatening attack was made on me.” A DJ was accompanying the visarjan procession According to local residents, the Ganesha idol visarjan procession had set off from Bakhira town. The procession was heading towards Dhodhaya Canal via Amardobha. Just then, Mehndawal CO Sarvdaman Singh arrived at the spot. It is alleged that the CO took photographs of the DJ vehicle accompanying the procession and spoke of taking it to the Bakhira police station. Outraged by this, the people participating in the procession sat on the road in protest. It was during this time that the mob attacked the MP's vehicle. Following the attack on the MP's vehicle, the occupants inside it were also enraged. They sat on the road and raised slogans against the police and administration. Officers from the police and administration reached the spot and brought the situation under control. The MP stated: Stones were pelted after seeing the party flag The MP said, "I was returning after meeting flood victims and other people. I was stuck in a traffic jam at the crossing. Just then, slogans of 'Pappu Nishad Murdabad' started being raised. Seeing the party flag, people began hurling bricks and stones at the vehicle. I got out of the car and ran towards the market to save my life. When the police saw the vehicles being vandalised, they resorted to a lathi charge. I somehow reached the police station and went home from there."

stories.title: Lucknow’s Papermill Colony has cleanest air in India:70 parks; residents formed groups, planted trees with own money
stories.summary: An unique initiative by residents of Lucknow's Paper Mill Ward has made the entire city proud. The residents formed groups, raised funds and created gardens in every home. The ward is numbered 70 in the municipal corporation. Working with the municipal corporation, they built 70 parks across the area. The project took around 20 years. But the results have now emerged. Paper Mill secured the number one rank in the Ministry of Environment's Air Survey 2026. This means its air is the cleanest in the country. The residents have created vertical gardens in the parks and planted trees using the Miyawaki method. Waste in the ward is collected only using electric vehicles. As a result, air pollution here is nearly zero. The ward has a population of around 60,000. Residents here say, The title of having the cleanest air in the country was not achieved in a single day. We worked hard for years to achieve it and paid attention to cleanliness. This result has come from caring for the ward together. How is the air in the ward so clean? To find out, a Bhaskar reporter surveyed the neighbourhoods. The survey found that the ward has remarkable greenery. It has beautiful parks, trees along the roads and no piles of rubbish anywhere. Homes of all sizes have gardens. The drains are clean, and the roads are free of dust. Five pictures of the ward with the cleanest air in the country- Extent of Papermill Colony Ward: Residents said: Prabha Chaturvedi also contributed to this recognition Prabha Chaturvedi, a resident of the ward, is no longer alive, but people are now praising her work after the ward received the honour. Residents say Prabha had launched a campaign to increase greenery in the ward. Shekhar Malviya said people here had developed the area using their own money. Prabha Chaturvedi was among them. Her efforts transformed the condition of the parks. People became aware of environmental issues. The ‘Greenery in Every Home’ campaign was launched. Work was undertaken on rainwater harvesting and making compost through kitchen-waste management. She initiated these efforts along with providing training. She also worked with women on cleanliness. She died in 2021 during the coronavirus pandemic, but people are now remembering her work. Her family currently lives abroad. 3 major reasons behind the country's cleanest air title Vertical gardens and Miyawaki gardening reduced air pollution Vertical gardens, plantation along roads and riverbanks, and forests developed using the Miyawaki method are being created in the ward to reduce air pollution. Urmila Van and Shakti Van are among the prominent ones. Encroachments and garbage are being removed along the Kukrail river, after which plants are being planted using the Miyawaki method. These forests have improved the air quality in the ward. They have also enhanced the beauty of the area. The parks have been landscaped properly. Better maintenance has further improved their appearance. This has increased the greenery in the area and cleaned the air. Water is sprayed every day to prevent dust from becoming airborne Water is sprinkled daily in the ward to prevent PM-10 pollution particles generated by road dust. As part of efforts to raise awareness, nets are installed at construction sites to contain construction and demolition waste. These nets are later removed properly. Roads within the ward are cleaned more effectively. All major roads are cleaner. In addition, the drains and smaller open drains are covered. PNG lines have been installed for clean fuel in large parts of the ward, including Nehru Enclave and Vishwas Khand. LPG is also used in homes across the ward. Electric vehicles collect waste, with real-time tracking through GPS Electric vehicles (e-auto tippers) have been introduced in place of the old diesel waste-collection vehicles. GPS has been installed in all the vehicles, and a control command centre has been set up for their real-time monitoring. This has improved waste collection in the ward. Waste is no longer piling up inside homes or on the roads. It is not dumped in the open. Waste is collected at only two compactor stations. These are located at Mithaiwala Chauraha and Metro City police outpost. Dustbins have also been placed at various locations in the neighbourhoods. Sewer and water pipelines have been laid throughout the ward, providing convenience to residents. What residents of the ward with the cleanest air have to say- The councillor heeds the elderly, while residents contributed their own money Shekhar Malviya said that for the past several years, elderly residents have been sitting on chairs by the roadside with the councillor from the morning and informing him about the work that needs to be done. Local councillor Rajesh Singh Gabbar implements it. There is greenery around every house here. The colony is old. Its residents have improved it with their own money, so work has continued to be carried out. This is not a one-day effort. Residents work themselves to keep the ward clean Girish Chandra Tiwari said that our ward ranked number one in the country. The biggest reason for this is the parks in our area. They are all clean and well-maintained. People here keep the areas around them clean and tidy. They work towards this themselves. The parks have facilities ranging from exercise equipment to other amenities, which help people stay close to nature. People are called out when they make mistakes; the change did not happen in a day Swati said that the people in her ward are hardworking. No other ward has as much greenery as this colony. The reason the colony is clean and beautiful is that everyone is working towards this with awareness. If anyone makes a mistake, they are stopped from doing so. Residents are also partners, but sanitation workers deserve praise Hemendra Singh Rawat said, I have been living in the colony for 60 years. Relentless efforts have been under way for 20 years. Work has been carried out for the ward since Rajesh Singh became the councillor. The public also contributes to these efforts. Construction and demolition waste is being stored properly. Besides us, we congratulate the workers who work from morning to keep the city clean. Councillor says - made possible by public awareness Rajesh Singh Gabbar, councillor for the Papermill Colony ward, said, Under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), the Papermill Colony ward has been ranked No. 1 in the country among wards with a population of more than 30,000 in the Swachh Vayu Survey 2025-26. This has been made possible by the cooperation and awareness of the people in the area. It was my dream for our ward to become the most beautiful ward in the country, with clean air and cleanliness. That has now become possible. I am grateful to all the people for this. For the past 20 years, the people have been guiding me. We have all continued to work together accordingly. This is why we have received this distinction. Congratulations to everyone. Three more pictures of the ward-

stories.title: Ayush says, ‘I will marry Chandni at any cost’:Court approves marriage; her family says they were framed in Shamli
stories.summary: Ayush Malik, a resident of Shamli, told the Allahabad High Court that he had embraced Islam of his own free will. Ayush also expressed his desire to marry his girlfriend, Chandni Qureshi. The court permitted him to do so and said, An adult cannot be prevented from making decisions regarding their religion, residence and choice of life partner solely on the grounds of family opposition. Ayush's father is a prominent medicine trader in the city. A photograph of Ayush wearing a skullcap and offering namaz had gone viral. Hindu organisations protested after this. Ayush's father accused Chandni Qureshi of forcing him to convert. The police also sent several people, including Chandni and her father, to jail. After the court's ruling, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Chandni's family. Read the report... Chandni's aunt's sons were also sent to jail Our team reached the home of Chandni Qureshi, who lives in Azad Chowk. We met Chandni's sister there. She said their father had gone to the market and that her elder sister was in Noida. Chandni's aunt's house is 100 metres from their home. Her aunt's son Mohammed Salim, her brother Tausif and some neighbours were sitting there. Tausif was also sent to jail in this case. Mohammad Salim said, Chandni is my maternal uncle's daughter. The Bharat Medical Store is 2 km from her home. Devraj Malik's son, Ayush Malik, used to sit there. There is a hospital next door where Chandni worked as a physiotherapist. Ayush used to bring his mother there. Ayush was the one who tried to trap Chandni. Maternal cousin said: Ayush trapped Chandni Mohammad Salim said that Chandni had made it clear from the outset: ‘We are Muslims. You are Jats. We have nothing to do with you and no relationship with you. Nor do we want any ties with you.’ Despite this, Devraj Malik had us framed as part of a conspiracy. He used Chandni as a pawn. He had us falsely implicated and sent to jail. He dragged not only us into the case, but also the family's elder paternal uncle, younger paternal uncle, maternal aunt's sons and the entire family. What is our fault? If we had even the slightest role or fault in this case, they could have shot us at a crossroads. Salim said - If she had wanted to frame him, she could have had a court marriage Salim said that if Chandni had really wanted to frame Ayush, she could have had a court marriage with him, but she did not do so. The boy had been converting to Islam and growing a beard for 12 years - did his father and family not know about it? Even the brothers and paternal aunt's sons have been framed in the case. How could people who cannot sign arrange a nikah? We have been rendered homeless. The locks on our house were broken and the police and administration were let inside; people entered the house by jumping from the roof. This is outright oppression against poor people like us. If the same oppression had happened to someone else, what would they have gone through? Shamli SP Narendra Pratap Singh said that the matter is before the court. The police are not intervening in the matter at present. Action will be taken if any complaint is received. Now, know the full story Devraj Malik, a resident of Dayanand Nagar, is the president of the Chemists Association in Shamli district. He owns a house in the city's upscale area and two well-known medical stores in the city. His two daughters are married. His son, Ayush Malik, ran a medical store after completing a BPharm. On 6 June, Devraj Malik lodged a report at the Kotwali police station. He alleged that Chandni Qureshi had lured his son into a relationship and had him converted. She had his name changed to Mohammed Ali. Ayush had suddenly started changing his appearance. He first grew a beard and then began going to the mosque. A photograph of Ayush also surfaced, showing him offering prayers at a mosque. He was seen sitting at the medical store wearing a skullcap and a kurta-pyjama. FIR filed after protests by Hindu organisations Swami Yashveer, the mahant of Yog Sadhana Ashram, released a video. He said that Chandni Qureshi had trapped the only son of the owner of Bharat Medical Store. Under pressure, the entire family had converted to another religion. After the matter came to light, Hindu organisations began protesting and threatened to stage a sit-in outside Chandni's house. Police had registered an FIR against eight people in the case, including Chandni Qureshi, her father Islam Qureshi and three maulvis. On 7 June, police arrested three accused, including Chandni Qureshi and her father. After spending one and a half months in judicial custody, the father and daughter were granted bail by the court on 24 July. He became a Hindu again after performing religious rituals just 15 days later About 15 days later, Ayush released a video. He said, Mother, seeing your distress, I have returned of my own accord to my original religion, Hinduism. Please forgive me. On 9 September, Ayush's friend Mohammad Sultan filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court. He alleged that Ayush was being forcibly confined at home. The court ordered Ayush's father to produce him before the court on 16 September. Expressed desire to convert to Islam before the court On 16 September, Ayush Malik was produced before a bench of the Allahabad High Court headed by Justice Sandeep Jain. Ayush said, I am around 31 years old. I have studied up to BPharm. I converted to Islam of my own free will in 2014. I want to marry Chandni Qureshi. My father and family do not approve of this decision. Ayush alleged that he had received threats and had been kept under house arrest since June 2026. His father, Devraj Malik, rejected all his son's allegations outright. He said that some people had ‘brainwashed’ his son. As a father, he is deeply concerned about his son's future. Court says Ayush has the right to make his own decisions The court said Ayush Malik is an adult and fully capable of making decisions about his own life. It said he had converted his religion of his own free will, without any pressure or threats, and had decided to marry Chandni Qureshi. The court acknowledged that it was natural for Devraj Singh Malik to be concerned as a father. However, this concern cannot override the constitutional rights of an adult citizen. Therefore, Ayush has the independent right to live with a person of his choice according to his wishes, practise his religion and make decisions regarding marriage in accordance with the law. Father says-he will remain my son After the High Court's order, father Devraj Malik said that Ayush Malik is and will remain his son. He cannot live without his son. The High Court's decision is acceptable to him. ‘I want Ayush to live with his family.’ However, no statement from Ayush Malik has emerged in the matter so far.
